Avoid expanding endpoint access based only on a callback’s arrival.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Handover field</th> <th>Why it matters</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Message and recipient IDs</strong></td> <td>Correlate the planned delivery</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Observed interaction</strong></td> <td>Describe the event without assuming identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Endpoint identity</strong></td> <td>Confirm the approved asset where relevant</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Process and token context</strong></td> <td>Bound any execution claim</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Allowed next action</strong></td> <td>Prevent automatic expansion beyond the test</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-the-simulation-overview"> <a href="#watch-the-simulation-overview" title="Watch the Simulation Overview">Watch the Simulation Overview</a> <a href="#watch-the-simulation-overview" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch the Simulation Overview">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Microsoft Security’s overview</strong> introduces Attack Simulation Training and its measurement purpose. Watch for how simulation outcomes lead to targeted learning and subsequent evaluation. Compare the presentation’s metrics with the denominator and ambiguity checks above.</p> <p><em>The video is an introductory 2021 presentation. Consult current product documentation for availability, UI details, and event semantics.</em></p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/zB_O-6bwZbc/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="zB_O-6bwZbc" videotitle="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/zB_O-6bwZbc\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Watch on YouTube:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="design-your-test-specification"> <a href="#design-your-test-specification" title="Design Your Test Specification">Design Your Test Specification</a> <a href="#design-your-test-specification" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Design Your Test Specification">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Create a specification</strong> for an inert link simulation using synthetic recipients. Define delivery evidence, a user-interaction criterion, an automated-event review rule, and a reporting objective. State explicitly which execution and access questions the simulation leaves unanswered.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Test ID and approved objective: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Recipients and excluded groups: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Sending service and artifact revision: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Landing-page behavior and collected fields: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Delivery window and stopping conditions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Delivery evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Interaction evidence and automation review: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Reporting metric and denominator: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Technical-control exceptions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Unexpected-recipient handling: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Retention, owner, and follow-up: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Evaluate the design</strong> by applying it to the worked dataset. Another reader should reproduce the four rates and explain the remaining uncertainty. Revise any metric which labels a click as endpoint compromise without separate evidence.</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Stages:</strong> why is message delivery insufficient proof of execution?</li> <li><strong>Automation:</strong> what else generates a recorded link interaction?</li> <li><strong>Comparison:</strong> why does message difficulty matter when comparing rates?</li> <li><strong>Architecture:</strong> does a 64-bit OS prove the current process is 64-bit?</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Stages</strong></td> <td>Client, application, policy, and user-action boundaries remain</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Automation</strong></td> <td>Security inspection, link analysis, and other automated processing</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Comparison</strong></td> <td>The recipient’s recognition task changed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Architecture</strong></td> <td>A 32-bit process also runs on supported 64-bit Windows systems</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Host awareness</strong> establishes what an approved starting context contains. Continue to <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 11: Situational Awareness and Host Operations"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/situational-awareness-and-host-operations/"> <a href="/red-team-course/situational-awareness-and-host-operations/" rel="follow me" >Module 11: Situational Awareness and Host Operations</a> </span> for identity, process, network, and freshness checks. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course hub</a> </span> for the full sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 11: Situational Awareness and Host Operations
item.description: Build a current host-state record using Windows and Linux identity, process, socket, and routing evidence, with a worked snapshot comparison.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Situational awareness</strong> is a current, evidence-backed picture of the host and security context where an assessment action would run. It starts with identity and scope, then adds the process, network, and service facts needed for the next decision. Collecting every available field is less useful than answering the right questions accurately.</p> <p><em>Allow about 18 minutes, plus time to create the host-state record. Commands below inspect local state and do not require credential extraction.</em></p> <h2 id="what-you-will-learn"> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" title="What You Will Learn">What You Will Learn</a> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What You Will Learn">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Identify</strong> the host, account, process, and network context separately.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> why an interface address does not establish a usable route.</li> <li><strong>Apply</strong> read-only Windows or Linux checks in a training environment.</li> <li><strong>Analyze</strong> changes between two host snapshots.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a handover record with freshness and collection limits.</li> </ul> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Host identity</strong></td> <td>Evidence tying the current system to an approved asset</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Security context</strong></td> <td>Identity and permissions used by the current process or thread</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>PID</strong></td> <td>Process identifier, valid within its host and lifetime</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Listener</strong></td> <td>Socket accepting incoming communication</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Route</strong></td> <td>Rule selecting how traffic reaches a destination</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Snapshot</strong></td> <td>Observations collected during a stated time window</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="establish-identity-before-interpretation"> <a href="#establish-identity-before-interpretation" title="Establish Identity Before Interpretation">Establish Identity Before Interpretation</a> <a href="#establish-identity-before-interpretation" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Establish Identity Before Interpretation">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A hostname or IP address</strong> is one part of an identity check. Match it against the approved inventory and available asset identifiers. DHCP changes, aliases, cloned lab systems, and virtual interfaces make a single label insufficient in some environments.</p> <p><strong>The account context</strong> is a separate fact. A visible desktop user, a remote session’s user, and a service account need not be the same principal. Reuse the SID and token distinctions from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 4"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/foundations-windows-internals-and-authentication/"> <a href="/red-team-course/foundations-windows-internals-and-authentication/" rel="follow me" >Module 4</a> </span> before interpreting access results.</p> <p><strong>Freshness</strong> belongs beside each observation. A process list gathered before a service restart does not describe the replacement process. Record the collection window and repeat only the checks invalidated by a relevant state change.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Evidence</th> <th>Common shortcut to avoid</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Which host?</strong></td> <td>Inventory match plus local identifiers</td> <td>One familiar name</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which account?</strong></td> <td>Current identity and authority</td> <td>Visible desktop owner</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which process?</strong></td> <td>PID, image, start time, and context</td> <td>Process filename alone</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>When observed?</strong></td> <td>Timestamp and collection window</td> <td>Undated pasted output</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="build-a-minimal-snapshot"> <a href="#build-a-minimal-snapshot" title="Build a Minimal Snapshot">Build a Minimal Snapshot</a> <a href="#build-a-minimal-snapshot" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build a Minimal Snapshot">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Choose fields by purpose.</strong> Before a local configuration check, you need the current account and target object’s context. Before interpreting an outbound connection, you need the source process, route, destination, and relevant time. These questions call for different snapshots.</p> <p><strong>Collection itself is activity.</strong> Native commands, scripts, and in-process extensions differ in implementation, but all require evidence appropriate to their behavior. Avoid assuming a BOF is automatically quiet or a built-in executable automatically safe for any workload.</p> <p><strong>Missing information</strong> should stay visible. Permissions, process termination, tool filtering, and collection failures all affect completeness. Record “not collected” or “access denied” when appropriate rather than replacing uncertainty with an empty field.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/host-identity-process-network-snapshot.webp", "caption": "Four boxes organize host identity, security context, process and socket observations, and a time-bounded operator decision", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.691972684 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.249673005", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.691972684 +0000 UTC m=+499.249673005"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/host-identity-process-network-snapshot.webp" alt="Four boxes organize host identity, security context, process and socket observations, and a time-bounded operator decision"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Refresh the fields affected by a change before relying on the snapshot</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="inspect-windows-identity"> <a href="#inspect-windows-identity" title="Inspect Windows Identity">Inspect Windows Identity</a> <a href="#inspect-windows-identity" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect Windows Identity">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start with local identity</strong> in a Windows training shell. <strong><code>hostname</code></strong> prints the computer name, <strong><code>whoami /user</code></strong> includes the current user SID, and <strong><code>whoami /groups</code></strong> shows group information for the current context. Compare the result with the approved inventory and account. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the whoami reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/whoami"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/whoami" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the whoami reference</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>hostname </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>whoami /user </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>whoami /groups </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ipconfig /all </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>ipconfig /all</code></strong> displays detailed adapter configuration. Read the adapter names, addresses, masks, gateways, and DNS settings together. An address alone does not prove a network is reachable or in scope. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the ipconfig reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/ipconfig"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/ipconfig" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the ipconfig reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Identity and network fields</strong> need separate interpretation. A domain account does not establish organizational ownership of every listed network. A successful local identity query also does not establish the account’s permissions on a remote resource.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Output field</th> <th>Use in the snapshot</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Computer name</strong></td> <td>Correlation with approved asset records</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Account SID</strong></td> <td>Stable identity reference within its authority</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Group state</strong></td> <td>Context for later permission interpretation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Adapter and gateway</strong></td> <td>Starting point for route analysis</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="correlate-processes-and-sockets"> <a href="#correlate-processes-and-sockets" title="Correlate Processes and Sockets">Correlate Processes and Sockets</a> <a href="#correlate-processes-and-sockets" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Correlate Processes and Sockets">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Process and connection lists</strong> provide complementary observations. <strong><code>tasklist /v</code></strong> adds verbose process information, while <strong><code>netstat -ano</code></strong> displays connections and listeners numerically with associated PIDs. Read both during a short collection window. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read tasklist"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/tasklist"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/tasklist" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read tasklist</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="netstat"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/netstat"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/netstat" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >netstat</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>tasklist /v </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>netstat -ano </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Flag meanings:</strong> <strong><code>/v</code></strong> requests verbose task information. For netstat, <strong><code>-a</code></strong> includes connections and listening endpoints, <strong><code>-n</code></strong> keeps numeric addresses and ports, and <strong><code>-o</code></strong> includes the owning PID. These flags inspect state rather than proving application purpose.</p> <p><strong>PID correlation has a time boundary.</strong> A process might exit between commands, and a later process might reuse its identifier. Include image path and start-time evidence where available before joining records from distant timestamps.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Socket observation</th> <th>Interpretation limit</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Loopback listener</strong></td> <td>Local binding does not establish remote exposure</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Wildcard listener</strong></td> <td>Listening scope does not prove firewall permission</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Established connection</strong></td> <td>Connection state does not establish authorized application behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>PID match</strong></td> <td>Correlate within the correct host and process lifetime</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="use-process-explorer-carefully"> <a href="#use-process-explorer-carefully" title="Use Process Explorer Carefully">Use Process Explorer Carefully</a> <a href="#use-process-explorer-carefully" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Use Process Explorer Carefully">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Process Explorer</strong> adds an interactive view of running processes, handles, DLLs, and mapped files. Its lower-pane modes help connect a selected process with resources it has opened. Use this to investigate a specific question rather than treating a large tree as a conclusion. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Microsoft’s Process Explorer overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/process-explorer"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/process-explorer" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Microsoft’s Process Explorer overview</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>A useful observation</strong> includes the selected process, timestamp, relevant properties, and what the view establishes. An image with a familiar name still needs context such as path, signer information, parentage, and behavior. A signature is evidence about provenance, not a blanket approval of every action.</p> <p><strong>Pavel Yosifovich’s demonstration</strong> explains Process Explorer features in Microsoft’s Sysinternals series. Watch for the distinction between process identity and loaded resources. Then choose one view which would improve your own host-state record.</p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Sysinternals: Process Explorer deep dive (demo) | ProcExp, DLL, Windows | Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/ZqZvzA4OGDA/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZqZvzA4OGDA"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="ZqZvzA4OGDA" videotitle="Sysinternals: Process Explorer deep dive (demo) | ProcExp, DLL, Windows | Microsoft" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZqZvzA4OGDA" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Sysinternals: Process Explorer deep dive (demo) | ProcExp, DLL, Windows | Microsoft"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Sysinternals: Process Explorer deep dive (demo) | ProcExp, DLL, Windows | Microsoft", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/ZqZvzA4OGDA\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZqZvzA4OGDA", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Watch on YouTube:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Sysinternals: Process Explorer deep dive"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZqZvzA4OGDA"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZqZvzA4OGDA" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Sysinternals: Process Explorer deep dive</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="inspect-linux-context"> <a href="#inspect-linux-context" title="Inspect Linux Context">Inspect Linux Context</a> <a href="#inspect-linux-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect Linux Context">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Kernel and distribution identity</strong> answer different questions. <strong><code>uname -a</code></strong> reports kernel and machine information, while <strong><code>/etc/os-release</code></strong> provides distribution identification fields on systems implementing this interface. Neither replaces a package inventory or patch assessment. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read uname"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/uname.1.html"> <a href="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/uname.1.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read uname</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="os-release"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/os-release.5.html"> <a href="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/os-release.5.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >os-release</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>id </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>uname -a </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cat /etc/os-release </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ip address show </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ip route show </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ss -lnt </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>id</code></strong> reports user and group identity for the invoking context. <strong><code>ip address show</code></strong> lists address assignments, and <strong><code>ip route show</code></strong> displays routes in the default listing context. More complex policy routing requires additional interpretation beyond this initial view. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the address"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ip-address.8.html"> <a href="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ip-address.8.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the address</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="route"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ip-route.8.html"> <a href="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ip-route.8.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >route</a> </span> references.</p> <p><strong><code>ss -lnt</code></strong> displays listening TCP sockets using numeric values. <strong><code>-l</code></strong> selects listeners, <strong><code>-n</code></strong> avoids service-name resolution, and <strong><code>-t</code></strong> selects TCP. Add process information only when needed and available under the current permissions. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the ss reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ss.8.html"> <a href="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ss.8.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the ss reference</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Linux evidence</th> <th>Useful distinction</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>User and groups</strong></td> <td>Current identity versus another logged-in session</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Kernel release</strong></td> <td>Kernel information versus distribution branding</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Addresses</strong></td> <td>Assigned interfaces versus reachable destinations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Routes</strong></td> <td>Selected forwarding path versus permitted application access</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Listening socket</strong></td> <td>Bound endpoint versus an external reachability result</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="avoid-the-two-address-shortcut"> <a href="#avoid-the-two-address-shortcut" title="Avoid the Two-Address Shortcut">Avoid the Two-Address Shortcut</a> <a href="#avoid-the-two-address-shortcut" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Avoid the Two-Address Shortcut">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Multiple addresses</strong> do not automatically make a host a bridge into another network. One interface might have several addresses, a VPN might contribute a route, or a virtual interface might belong to a local container network. Identify the interface type and routing context before drawing a topology conclusion.</p> <p><strong>Forwarding</strong> is another condition. A host having interfaces on two networks does not establish forwarding between them. Routes, forwarding settings, firewall policy, and application behavior determine which communication is possible.</p> <p><strong>Authorization remains independent.</strong> Learning about another network does not make it part of the assessment. Record the relationship as an unresolved topology observation and ask the agreed owner to confirm the permitted next step.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Follow-up question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Second address</strong></td> <td>Same interface, different interface, or virtual endpoint?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Additional route</strong></td> <td>Which destinations and policy context use it?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Two connected networks</strong></td> <td>Is forwarding enabled and permitted?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>New reachable service</strong></td> <td>Is the asset and proposed action in scope?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="work-a-snapshot-difference"> <a href="#work-a-snapshot-difference" title="Work a Snapshot Difference">Work a Snapshot Difference</a> <a href="#work-a-snapshot-difference" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Work a Snapshot Difference">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative scenario:</strong> at 09:00, PID 4200 runs the approved training service and listens on loopback port 8765. At 09:10, PID 4200 belongs to a different program, while the training service has PID 6100. Its replacement listener binds to all IPv4 interfaces.</p> <p><strong>Analyze the change:</strong> identify which old observations are stale and which new exposure question needs validation. Decide whether the PID reuse proves the original process changed its identity. Keep process lifetime and socket binding separate in your answer.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> the 09:00 PID-to-process association is stale. The new program’s reuse of PID 4200 does not make it the same process. The binding change warrants a scoped reachability review, but it does not prove the service is reachable through every firewall or network path.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence needed</th> <th>Purpose</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Process start times</strong></td> <td>Distinguish old and replacement processes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Image and service association</strong></td> <td>Identify the new service instance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Current socket binding</strong></td> <td>Confirm the changed local endpoint</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Approved external check</strong></td> <td>Determine reachability from the relevant source</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="keep-privilege-claims-precise"> <a href="#keep-privilege-claims-precise" title="Keep Privilege Claims Precise">Keep Privilege Claims Precise</a> <a href="#keep-privilege-claims-precise" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Keep Privilege Claims Precise">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Elevated privileges</strong> affect available operations but do not prove any particular credential material is present. Authentication method, logon state, operating-system protections, and configuration all matter. Microsoft’s Credential Guard documentation describes isolation of certain secrets using virtualization-based security. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the Credential Guard overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/credential-guard/"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/credential-guard/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the Credential Guard overview</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Credential extraction</strong> is a separate assessment action, not a required step in a basic host snapshot. A host-awareness objective is often satisfied by identity, process, network, and service observations. Keep the collected fields tied to the actual decision.</p> <p><strong>Read-only does not mean free of effects.</strong> An expansive query still consumes resources and produces activity. Bound repeated collection by need, particularly on systems with strict availability requirements.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Claim</th> <th>More precise record</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>“Administrator means all secrets available”</strong></td> <td>Current privileges observed, credential availability untested</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>“No output means no process”</strong></td> <td>Query returned no record under the stated context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>“Two addresses mean a pivot”</strong></td> <td>Additional address observed, route and permission unresolved</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="create-a-host-state-record"> <a href="#create-a-host-state-record" title="Create a Host-State Record">Create a Host-State Record</a> <a href="#create-a-host-state-record" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create a Host-State Record">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Your deliverable</strong> is a concise snapshot for one disposable Windows or Linux system. Collect the smallest set of fields needed to explain its identity, current context, one process, and one socket. Include an explicit freshness limit or event which would invalidate the record.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Approved asset and inventory reference: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Collection start/end time: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Host and account identity: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Current process architecture and security context: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Relevant process PID, image, and start time: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Relevant adapter, route, and socket: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Command or tool version: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Raw output location: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Missing fields or access limitations: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Change which requires a refresh: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Supported next action: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Review the record</strong> by handing it to another reader. They should identify what is known, which facts are time-sensitive, and what remains untested. Avoid turning a snapshot into a permanent description of the host.</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Identity:</strong> why is a hostname insufficient in some environments?</li> <li><strong>Processes:</strong> what makes a PID-only correlation unreliable over time?</li> <li><strong>Networks:</strong> why do two addresses fail to prove forwarding?</li> <li><strong>Linux:</strong> which source distinguishes distribution identity from kernel information?</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Identity</strong></td> <td>Names, aliases, and cloned systems require inventory correlation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Processes</strong></td> <td>PIDs are reused after process exit</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Networks</strong></td> <td>Address assignment, routing, forwarding, and policy are separate conditions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Linux</strong></td> <td>os-release provides distribution identification fields</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>User persistence</strong> introduces changes whose trigger, identity, and removal need separate evidence. Continue to <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 12: User Persistence"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/user-persistence/"> <a href="/red-team-course/user-persistence/" rel="follow me" >Module 12: User Persistence</a> </span> to examine the lifecycle of a user-context startup entry. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course hub</a> </span> for the full sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 12: User Persistence
item.description: Understand user startup triggers, HKCU context, and restoration. Follow a benign Notepad Run-entry lab with evidence and cleanup checks.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>User persistence</strong> arranges for an action to recur in a user’s context after a defined trigger. A configuration entry, a successful launch, and a verified removal are three separate outcomes. This module uses a visible Notepad startup entry in a disposable Windows VM to examine the complete lifecycle.</p> <p><em>Allow about 20 minutes, plus two lab sign-ins. Use a dedicated test account and save your work before signing out.</em></p> <h2 id="what-you-will-learn"> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" title="What You Will Learn">What You Will Learn</a> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What You Will Learn">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Distinguish</strong> logon-triggered startup from boot-triggered services.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> user identity, executable availability, and policy dependencies.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> startup configuration before changing it.</li> <li><strong>Observe</strong> a benign entry through creation, trigger, and removal.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a lifecycle record with independent cleanup evidence.</li> </ul> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Startup entry</strong></td> <td>Configuration requesting execution at a defined trigger</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Run value</strong></td> <td>Named registry value specifying a command at user logon</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>RunOnce value</strong></td> <td>Startup configuration intended for a single logon execution</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>HKCU</strong></td> <td>HKEY_CURRENT_USER, resolved for the calling context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Trigger</strong></td> <td>Event which makes the configured action eligible to run</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Restoration</strong></td> <td>Return to the recorded baseline with verification</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="define-the-persistence-requirement"> <a href="#define-the-persistence-requirement" title="Define the Persistence Requirement">Define the Persistence Requirement</a> <a href="#define-the-persistence-requirement" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Define the Persistence Requirement">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Persistence is optional</strong> unless the assessment objective requires it. A short test with a controlled starting context might have no reason to create a recurring action. If recurrence is needed, define the trigger, account, duration, and removal owner before choosing a mechanism.</p> <p><strong>A Run entry uses logon</strong>, so a reboot without the relevant user signing in is not a complete test. A service with automatic startup follows a different lifecycle. User persistence also does not automatically increase the account’s permissions. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Microsoft’s Run and RunOnce documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/setupapi/run-and-runonce-registry-keys"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/setupapi/run-and-runonce-registry-keys" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Microsoft’s Run and RunOnce documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Configuration success</strong> proves only the entry was written. The referenced executable must exist, the relevant user must encounter the trigger, and policy must permit the resulting action. Separate those dependencies in both your test and your report.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Mechanism</th> <th>Trigger context</th> <th>Question to verify</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>User Run value</strong></td> <td>Relevant user’s logon</td> <td>Which user hive and command?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>User Startup shortcut</strong></td> <td>Relevant user’s logon</td> <td>Which shortcut, target, and arguments?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Scheduled task</strong></td> <td>Configured trigger and principal</td> <td>Which conditions and execution identity?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Automatic service</strong></td> <td>Service-control startup behavior</td> <td>Which account, dependencies, and service state?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="resolve-the-user-context"> <a href="#resolve-the-user-context" title="Resolve the User Context">Resolve the User Context</a> <a href="#resolve-the-user-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Resolve the User Context">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>HKCU</strong> is context-dependent. It is not a universal alias for whichever person appears on the visible desktop. Record the calling account’s SID before interpreting a user startup entry. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Microsoft’s predefined-key reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/predefined-keys"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/predefined-keys" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Microsoft’s predefined-key reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Profile portability</strong> is also conditional. Even if a profile-management system carries a registry entry to another machine, the executable, path, architecture, and applicable policies still need to match. A roaming profile is not a guarantee of execution across the environment.</p> <p><strong>Scope your claim</strong> to the account and machine observed. A successful test for one user does not establish recurrence for every user on the host. Record machine-level and user-level startup locations separately.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/user-startup-trigger-and-restoration.webp", "caption": "Four connected boxes show the user baseline, named startup entry, logon execution evidence, and verified restoration of the original state", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.697920942 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.255621254", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.697920942 +0000 UTC m=+499.255621254"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/user-startup-trigger-and-restoration.webp" alt="Four connected boxes show the user baseline, named startup entry, logon execution evidence, and verified restoration of the original state"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Removing configuration and stopping a running process are different cleanup tasks</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="inspect-before-changing"> <a href="#inspect-before-changing" title="Inspect Before Changing">Inspect Before Changing</a> <a href="#inspect-before-changing" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect Before Changing">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start with read-only queries</strong> in the test account’s shell. The first command records the SID, while the second displays values under the user Run key. A missing key or an access error is a result to document, not permission to create unrelated configuration.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>whoami /user </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>reg query</code></strong> displays the selected key’s entries without changing them. The <strong><code>/v</code></strong> option, used later, restricts the request to a named value. Save the baseline output with the account and timestamp. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the reg-query reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-query"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-query" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the reg-query reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Autoruns</strong> provides a broader view of configured automatic-start locations. Select the appropriate user and inspect the Logon category, while recording any active filters. A hidden entry in a filtered view is not an absent entry. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the Autoruns documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/autoruns"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/autoruns" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the Autoruns documentation</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Baseline field</th> <th>Purpose</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Account SID</strong></td> <td>Identify the user context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Registry path and view</strong></td> <td>Reproduce the location inspected</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Existing value names</strong></td> <td>Avoid overwriting another entry</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Tool filters</strong></td> <td>Explain which entries the view omits</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Executable path</strong></td> <td>Establish the intended benign target</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="create-a-benign-lab-entry"> <a href="#create-a-benign-lab-entry" title="Create a Benign Lab Entry">Create a Benign Lab Entry</a> <a href="#create-a-benign-lab-entry" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create a Benign Lab Entry">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use native 64-bit PowerShell</strong> in a disposable 64-bit Windows VM with the dedicated account. This exercise assumes the Run key already exists and Notepad is installed at the checked system path. If either prerequisite is missing, use a prepared lab image rather than changing broader startup configuration.</p> <p><strong>The following code</strong> creates one visibly named value pointing to Notepad. It stops if the value already exists, checks the target file, and avoids a force-overwrite option. It does not copy an executable or contact a network endpoint.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$runPath = <span style="color:#e6db74">'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$valueName = <span style="color:#e6db74">'CourseLab-Notepad'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$notepadPath = Join-Path $env:SystemRoot <span style="color:#e6db74">'System32\notepad.exe'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$runKey = Get-Item -LiteralPath $runPath -ErrorAction Stop </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> ($runKey.GetValueNames() <span style="color:#f92672">-contains</span> $valueName) { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">throw</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'The lab value already exists. Review the baseline first.'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> (<span style="color:#f92672">-not</span> (Test-Path -LiteralPath $notepadPath -PathType Leaf)) { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">throw</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'The expected Notepad executable is missing.'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$expectedCommand = <span style="color:#e6db74">'"'</span> + $notepadPath + <span style="color:#e6db74">'"'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>New-ItemProperty -LiteralPath $runPath -Name $valueName ` </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -PropertyType String -Value $expectedCommand -ErrorAction Stop </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Parameter meanings:</strong> <strong><code>-LiteralPath</code></strong> uses the exact registry path, <strong><code>-Name</code></strong> selects the single new value, and <strong><code>-PropertyType String</code></strong> creates a string value. <strong><code>-Value</code></strong> stores the quoted command path, while <strong><code>-ErrorAction Stop</code></strong> prevents continuing past a reported error in the selected operation. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read New-ItemProperty"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/new-itemproperty?view=powershell-7.5"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/new-itemproperty?view=powershell-7.5" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read New-ItemProperty</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Verify the stored value</strong> before testing logon. The query should show the visible lab name and the intended quoted path. Recheck the account SID if you opened a different shell or changed credentials.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>reg query "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" /v CourseLab-Notepad </span></span></code></pre></div><h2 id="observe-the-logon-trigger"> <a href="#observe-the-logon-trigger" title="Observe the Logon Trigger">Observe the Logon Trigger</a> <a href="#observe-the-logon-trigger" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Observe the Logon Trigger">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Close existing Notepad windows</strong>, save the baseline and creation records, then sign out and back into the dedicated VM account. Observe whether a new Notepad instance appears and collect process evidence for the relevant window. Windows does not promise an immediate launch order for Run entries, so record the observation window rather than assuming a precise startup deadline.</p> <p><strong>Interpret the trigger carefully.</strong> Automatic application restoration or another startup entry also might launch Notepad. Correlate the new entry, the sign-in, and process evidence instead of treating a visible window as unique proof of its origin.</p> <p><strong>A missing launch</strong> calls for dependency checks. Verify the account, stored command, executable availability, startup policy, and recorded errors. Do not alter security settings merely to force the expected result.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Supported conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Registry value exists</strong></td> <td>Configuration creation succeeded</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Relevant logon occurred</strong></td> <td>The intended trigger was exercised</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>New process correlated</strong></td> <td>Execution evidence supports the tested path</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No visible window</strong></td> <td>Further evidence is needed to explain the outcome</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="verify-restoration-separately"> <a href="#verify-restoration-separately" title="Verify Restoration Separately">Verify Restoration Separately</a> <a href="#verify-restoration-separately" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Restoration Separately">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Removal starts with identity.</strong> Use the same test account and compare its SID with the creation record. Recreate the variables in the new PowerShell session, then verify the stored command still matches the lab entry before removing the named value.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$runPath = <span style="color:#e6db74">'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$valueName = <span style="color:#e6db74">'CourseLab-Notepad'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$notepadPath = Join-Path $env:SystemRoot <span style="color:#e6db74">'System32\notepad.exe'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$expectedCommand = <span style="color:#e6db74">'"'</span> + $notepadPath + <span style="color:#e6db74">'"'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$runKey = Get-Item -LiteralPath $runPath -ErrorAction Stop </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> ($runKey.GetValueNames() <span style="color:#f92672">-notcontains</span> $valueName) { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">throw</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'The lab value is absent. Reconcile the account and evidence.'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> ($runKey.GetValue($valueName) <span style="color:#f92672">-cne</span> $expectedCommand) { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">throw</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'The value changed. Review it before removal.'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Remove-ItemProperty -LiteralPath $runPath -Name $valueName -ErrorAction Stop </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $runPath).GetValueNames() <span style="color:#f92672">-contains</span> $valueName) { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">throw</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'The lab value is still present.'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>Remove-ItemProperty</code></strong> removes the selected value rather than the entire Run key. The prechecks protect against deleting an unexpected entry encountered during the exercise. Preserve the removal result and a fresh query. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Remove-ItemProperty"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/remove-itemproperty?view=powershell-7.5"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/remove-itemproperty?view=powershell-7.5" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Remove-ItemProperty</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Configuration removal does not terminate Notepad.</strong> Close the specific lab window normally, then repeat the sign-out and sign-in test. Confirm the value remains absent and no execution attributable to the lab entry recurs.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Cleanup layer</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Configuration</strong></td> <td>Named value absent in the correct user context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Running instance</strong></td> <td>Lab process or window closed normally</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Later trigger</strong></td> <td>No recurrence attributable to the removed entry</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Baseline</strong></td> <td>Unrelated startup entries preserved</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="understand-observation-limits"> <a href="#understand-observation-limits" title="Understand Observation Limits">Understand Observation Limits</a> <a href="#understand-observation-limits" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Understand Observation Limits">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Startup configuration is observable</strong> regardless of whether a native utility or in-process extension writes it. MITRE documents registry Run keys and Startup folders as established persistence locations. The delivery mechanism does not erase the resulting configuration. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read ATT&CK T1547.001"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/"> <a href="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read ATT&CK T1547.001</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>A familiar value name</strong> is not proof of legitimate ownership. Evaluate the command, path, signer information, installation context, and observed behavior together. A file timestamp also does not establish provenance or explain who created the startup entry.</p> <p><strong>Broader startup locations</strong> have different consequences. Winlogon configuration, service settings, and application-loading mechanisms affect different triggers and process contexts. Inspect them as distinct mechanisms rather than treating every autostart entry as an interchangeable Run value.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence type</th> <th>Useful question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Configuration record</strong></td> <td>What action is requested, for whom, and when?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>File identity</strong></td> <td>Which executable or document is referenced?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution record</strong></td> <td>Did the intended process run under the expected context?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Removal record</strong></td> <td>Was the specific change reversed and retested?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="work-a-failed-launch-case"> <a href="#work-a-failed-launch-case" title="Work a Failed-Launch Case">Work a Failed-Launch Case</a> <a href="#work-a-failed-launch-case" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Work a Failed-Launch Case">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative scenario:</strong> a user Run value appears in both the registry and Autoruns. After signing into another account, the reviewer sees no Notepad window and reports the persistence test failed. The original account’s hive still contains the lab entry.</p> <p><strong>Evaluate the report</strong> using trigger and identity evidence. Decide which part of the test was completed and which prerequisite was missed. Then write the narrowest justified next step.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> configuration creation was confirmed, but the intended user’s logon was not tested. Signing into another account does not exercise the same user Run entry. Resume the test in the original lab account or record the untested trigger as a limitation.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Case variation</th> <th>Expected next check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Wrong user signed in</strong></td> <td>Reconcile SID and user hive</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Correct user, missing executable</strong></td> <td>Confirm path and file availability</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Correct entry, delayed launch</strong></td> <td>Review the observation window and execution evidence</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Entry removed, window remains</strong></td> <td>Close the existing instance and test recurrence separately</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-the-autoruns-demonstration"> <a href="#watch-the-autoruns-demonstration" title="Watch the Autoruns Demonstration">Watch the Autoruns Demonstration</a> <a href="#watch-the-autoruns-demonstration" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch the Autoruns Demonstration">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Aaron Margosis’s Microsoft demonstration</strong> explains Autoruns and its startup views. Record the before-state, exact named change, trigger, evidence, removal, and later retest. If you stop before removal verification, leave the exercise open with a named owner.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Lab asset, account SID, and registry view: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Baseline timestamp and evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Value name, type, and exact command: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Creation result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Logon trigger and observation window: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Execution evidence and alternative explanations: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Removal result and fresh configuration query: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Existing process closure: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Later logon result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Remaining differences from baseline: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>A completed record</strong> proves more than a single screenshot of Notepad. Another reviewer should reconstruct the sequence and identify the evidence supporting restoration. Keep this record for the cleanup comparison in <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 15"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/persistence-cleanup-and-defense-evasion/"> <a href="/red-team-course/persistence-cleanup-and-defense-evasion/" rel="follow me" >Module 15</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Trigger:</strong> is a reboot without user logon a sufficient Run-entry test?</li> <li><strong>Identity:</strong> which account determines the HKCU context?</li> <li><strong>Portability:</strong> why does a copied profile entry not guarantee execution elsewhere?</li> <li><strong>Cleanup:</strong> does removing the value stop a running process?</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Trigger</strong></td> <td>The relevant user logon still needs to occur</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Identity</strong></td> <td>The calling security context, verified against the recorded SID</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Portability</strong></td> <td>Executable, path, policy, and environment dependencies remain</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Cleanup</strong></td> <td>Configuration removal and process termination are separate actions</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Local privilege escalation</strong> concerns crossing a permission boundary, which user persistence alone does not establish. Continue to <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 13: Local Privilege Escalation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/local-privilege-escalation/"> <a href="/red-team-course/local-privilege-escalation/" rel="follow me" >Module 13: Local Privilege Escalation</a> </span> to analyze prerequisites and supported impact. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course hub</a> </span> for the full sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 13: Local Privilege Escalation
item.description: Evaluate Windows privilege escalation paths through service permissions, DLL loading, evidence quality, and a read-only lab exercise.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Local privilege escalation</strong> crosses a permission boundary on a host. A writable directory, unusual service, or scanner finding starts an investigation. Establish which identity controls which operation, which privileged process consumes the result, and what evidence supports the claimed impact.</p> <p>This module develops a <strong>permission-boundary record</strong>. You will inspect a prepared training service without modifying it, compare incomplete findings, and design a minimal validation with a clear stopping point.</p> <p><em>Allow 35–50 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. The worked case is illustrative, not an observed compromise.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> service permissions, file permissions, and DLL search behavior.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> why a suspicious configuration is an incomplete escalation claim.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> a training service and its filesystem permissions.</li> <li><strong>Compare</strong> evidence for competing escalation hypotheses.</li> <li><strong>Produce</strong> a validation record with a remediation and retest condition.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>Use a <strong>disposable Windows lab VM</strong> with an instructor-provided service named <strong><code>CourseLabService</code></strong> and a documented application directory. Read <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Windows identity and tokens"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/foundations-windows-internals-and-authentication/"> <a href="/red-team-course/foundations-windows-internals-and-authentication/" rel="follow me" >Windows identity and tokens</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="host awareness"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/situational-awareness-and-host-operations/"> <a href="/red-team-course/situational-awareness-and-host-operations/" rel="follow me" >host awareness</a> </span> first. Run the inspection from the account whose permissions you intend to assess.</p> <p>If no training service exists, complete the <strong>paper exercise</strong> below. Do not substitute an unfamiliar production service. The inspection commands query state, while service installation, ACL changes, and restarts require a separate exercise specification.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Record before inspection</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Principal</strong></td> <td>Account SID, groups, integrity level, and relevant token privileges</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Object</strong></td> <td>Exact service name, executable path, and application version</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Boundary</strong></td> <td>Current rights and the additional operation under review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Trigger</strong></td> <td>Permitted event and its expected service impact</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>Timestamp, command result, trace location, and baseline owner</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="define-the-boundary"> <a href="#define-the-boundary" title="Define the Boundary">Define the Boundary</a> <a href="#define-the-boundary" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Define the Boundary">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>discretionary access control list</strong>, or DACL, specifies allowed and denied access entries on an object. Effective access depends on the requested operation and the caller’s token. Reading a configuration is different from changing it, and changing a file is different from replacing its containing directory.</p> <p>The <strong>service object</strong> and its executable are separate securable objects. Permission to query a service does not imply permission to reconfigure it. A service’s configuration, binary, and supporting directories therefore need separate evidence. Microsoft documents distinct service rights for querying, changing configuration, starting, and stopping a service. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Service access rights"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/services/service-security-and-access-rights"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/services/service-security-and-access-rights" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Service access rights</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence</th> <th>Meaning</th> <th>Missing conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Query succeeds</strong></td> <td>Configuration is readable</td> <td>Configuration is writable</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Directory is writable</strong></td> <td>Some filesystem operations are permitted</td> <td>Privileged code loads a controlled file</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Service uses LocalSystem</strong></td> <td>Configured service identity is highly privileged</td> <td>Your proposed input reaches its execution path</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Start is permitted</strong></td> <td>Caller has a trigger permission</td> <td>Caller controls the launched program</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="trace-the-whole-path"> <a href="#trace-the-whole-path" title="Trace the Whole Path">Trace the Whole Path</a> <a href="#trace-the-whole-path" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Trace the Whole Path">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/permission-boundary-evidence-chain.webp", "caption": "Four stages connect the current principal, controlled object, privileged consumer, and evidence needed to validate a Windows escalation path", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.703011795 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.260712126", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.703011795 +0000 UTC m=+499.260712126"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/permission-boundary-evidence-chain.webp" alt="Four stages connect the current principal, controlled object, privileged consumer, and evidence needed to validate a Windows escalation path"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Every link
