needs evidence before a configuration finding becomes an escalation result</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p>A useful <strong>escalation hypothesis</strong> names a chain: principal, permitted modification, privileged consumer, and trigger. One missing link changes the conclusion. The chain also reveals where a defender should break the dependency.</p> <p>Consider a training application’s <strong>plugin directory</strong>. An ordinary user writes files there, but the privileged service loads plugins only from a different, protected directory. The writable location deserves configuration review, yet it does not establish the proposed service escalation. Your report should preserve this distinction instead of promoting every weak permission into SYSTEM execution.</p> <blockquote> <p><strong>Evidence discipline:</strong> State the strongest supported claim, then name the next observation needed to strengthen it.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="inspect-the-training-service"> <a href="#inspect-the-training-service" title="Inspect the Training Service">Inspect the Training Service</a> <a href="#inspect-the-training-service" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect the Training Service">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>whoami.exe /all </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sc.exe qc CourseLabService </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sc.exe sdshow CourseLabService </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>whoami.exe /all</code></strong> records the inspection identity and token context. <strong><code>sc.exe qc</code></strong> reads the service configuration, including its configured executable and service account. <strong><code>sc.exe sdshow</code></strong> displays the service security descriptor, whose interpretation concerns the service object rather than its executable. Use <strong><code>sc.exe</code></strong> explicitly in PowerShell to avoid a command-name alias collision. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s sc qc reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/cc742055%28v%3Dws.11%29"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/cc742055%28v%3Dws.11%29" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s sc qc reference</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="sc sdshow reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/cc742133%28v%3Dws.11%29"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/cc742133%28v%3Dws.11%29" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >sc sdshow reference</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>icacls.exe <span style="color:#e6db74">"C:\CourseLab\Service"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>icacls.exe <span style="color:#e6db74">"C:\CourseLab\Service\CourseLabService.exe"</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>icacls.exe</code></strong> displays filesystem DACLs when invoked this way. Replace the example paths only with the instructor’s recorded lab paths. The commands do not grant permissions or establish which file a running process has loaded. Preserve both command output and error messages. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s icacls reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/icacls"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/icacls" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s icacls reference</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Result</th> <th>Next interpretation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Service absent</strong></td> <td>Check the lab manifest rather than inventing a target</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Access denied</strong></td> <td>Record the blocked query and current principal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Inherited permission</strong></td> <td>Identify its parent and affected objects before proposing a fix</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Path differs</strong></td> <td>Update the hypothesis to match the configured application</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Expected observation:</strong> Successful queries produce configuration and permissions for the prepared objects. No particular permission weakness is guaranteed. These Windows examples are documentation-reviewed, not execution-tested on the macOS authoring host.</p> <h2 id="interpret-tool-findings"> <a href="#interpret-tool-findings" title="Interpret Tool Findings">Interpret Tool Findings</a> <a href="#interpret-tool-findings" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Interpret Tool Findings">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>SharpUp</strong> is a C# assessment tool with checks for issues such as modifiable services, modifiable service binaries, unquoted service paths, and hijackable paths. Its repository distinguishes checks from weaponization. Record the source revision and selected check rather than treating an old screenshot as a stable interface. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GhostPack’s SharpUp repository"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/GhostPack/SharpUp"> <a href="https://github.com/GhostPack/SharpUp" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >GhostPack’s SharpUp repository</a> </span> .</p> <p>A <strong>checker result</strong> prioritizes manual review. An unquoted service path needs more analysis than the presence of a space. A writable PATH entry needs more analysis than a permissive ACL. Compare the tool’s assumptions with the exact process, filesystem layout, and operating-system build in your record.</p> <p><strong>Execution method</strong> also changes the observation surface. An external utility, managed assembly, and in-process BOF have different dependencies and failure boundaries. None guarantees silence, and an in-memory operation still invokes observable system behavior. Revisit <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Beacon execution and BOFs"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/beacon-execution-and-beacon-object-files/"> <a href="/red-team-course/beacon-execution-and-beacon-object-files/" rel="follow me" >Beacon execution and BOFs</a> </span> for compatibility and failure analysis before choosing a collection method.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Collection choice</th> <th>Question to answer first</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Native query</strong></td> <td>Which process and object access events are expected?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Managed checker</strong></td> <td>Which runtime, checks, and child processes does this version use?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>In-process component</strong></td> <td>What happens to the hosting process if the component fails?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Existing defender trace</strong></td> <td>Does its collection window cover the proposed behavior?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="understand-dll-loading"> <a href="#understand-dll-loading" title="Understand DLL Loading">Understand DLL Loading</a> <a href="#understand-dll-loading" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Understand DLL Loading">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>DLL search-order hijacking</strong> depends on actual loader behavior. Windows considers factors such as loaded modules, KnownDLLs, manifests, application type, and loader flags. PATH is only part of some search strategies. An arbitrary writable PATH directory does not guarantee selection. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s DLL search-order documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlls/dynamic-link-library-search-order"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlls/dynamic-link-library-search-order" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s DLL search-order documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p>A <strong>missing-file event</strong> is also incomplete evidence. Programs often probe optional files or continue searching after an unsuccessful lookup. Correlate the requested name, process identity, later lookup results, and the path ultimately loaded. Avoid publishing a named Windows DLL as a universal escalation route without a reproducible affected-version record.</p> <p>For ordinary native <strong>x86/x64 DLL loading</strong>, match the library to the loading process. A 64-bit operating system also runs 32-bit processes, so OS bitness alone is insufficient. The file’s expected exports and application behavior matter alongside architecture. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s process interoperability documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/process-interoperability"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/process-interoperability" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s process interoperability documentation</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Further evidence needed</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>NAME NOT FOUND</strong></td> <td>Whether the failed lookup affects a used code path</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Writable searched directory</strong></td> <td>Whether a controlled file would be selected before another copy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Compatible architecture</strong></td> <td>Required exports and successful application behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Privileged loader</strong></td> <td>Token context at the operation and an approved trigger</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-a-specific-case"> <a href="#watch-a-specific-case" title="Watch a Specific Case">Watch a Specific Case</a> <a href="#watch-a-specific-case" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch a Specific Case">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="300 Milliseconds to Admin: Mastering DLL Hijacking and Hooking to Win the Race"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/YwNcTuHxnAI/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwNcTuHxnAI"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="YwNcTuHxnAI" videotitle="300 Milliseconds to Admin: Mastering DLL Hijacking and Hooking to Win the Race" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwNcTuHxnAI" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="300 Milliseconds to Admin: Mastering DLL Hijacking and Hooking to Win the Race"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "300 Milliseconds to Admin: Mastering DLL Hijacking and Hooking to Win the Race", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/YwNcTuHxnAI\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwNcTuHxnAI", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Compass Security’s case study</strong> illustrates how application behavior and timing shape a DLL hijacking investigation. Treat its demonstrated conditions as specific to the researched case. It is supplemental analysis, not proof of vulnerability on every Windows installation. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch the presentation on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwNcTuHxnAI"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwNcTuHxnAI" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch the presentation on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <p>While watching, identify the <strong>controlled object</strong>, the privileged consumer, and the timing dependency. Then ask which observation would invalidate the proposed path. This exercise builds a stronger review habit than remembering a filename.</p> <h2 id="compare-three-findings"> <a href="#compare-three-findings" title="Compare Three Findings">Compare Three Findings</a> <a href="#compare-three-findings" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare Three Findings">#</a> </h2> <p>The following <strong>synthetic findings</strong> concern one training application. Assume the instructor supplied complete permission evidence for the stated objects, but no execution test has occurred. Your task is to rank the next investigation step without claiming successful escalation.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Finding</th> <th>Available evidence</th> <th>Defensible assessment</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>A: Writable cache</strong></td> <td>User modifies cache files, service never reads them</td> <td>No demonstrated privileged dependency</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>B: Writable plugin</strong></td> <td>User modifies a file read by a higher-privilege loader</td> <td>Strong candidate, loading semantics and trigger remain</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>C: Readable service</strong></td> <td>User queries a LocalSystem service with protected files</td> <td>Read access alone supplies no escalation path</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Finding B</strong> deserves the next bounded validation because the evidence connects user control to a privileged consumer. Request a prepared benign fixture from the application owner, define its expected marker, and agree on a trigger window. Do not substitute an unrestricted payload or reboot simply because an earlier lab used one.</p> <p>A <strong>negative result</strong> still needs interpretation. No marker after the trigger might reflect a failed load, a different path, a blocked action, or missing collection. Preserve the trace and separate these possibilities before closing the finding.</p> <h2 id="choose-the-smallest-proof"> <a href="#choose-the-smallest-proof" title="Choose the Smallest Proof">Choose the Smallest Proof</a> <a href="#choose-the-smallest-proof" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose the Smallest Proof">#</a> </h2> <p>A good <strong>validation plan</strong> answers one disputed question. If the dispute is whether the service reads a directory, a file-access trace might suffice. If the dispute is code execution under another identity, a mere file read is insufficient. Agree on the evidence threshold with the reviewer before changing the lab.</p> <p><strong>Operational cost</strong> belongs in the decision. Restarting a service, changing a dependency, or rebooting a host has different effects. A maintenance window does not automatically authorize every trigger. Prefer an owner-provided test application when production timing or recovery is uncertain.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Disputed claim</th> <th>Minimal useful evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Principal controls object</strong></td> <td>Effective permission result for the required operation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Consumer selects path</strong></td> <td>Correlated loader or application trace</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Boundary is crossed</strong></td> <td>Benign result tied to the higher-privilege execution context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Remediation breaks path</strong></td> <td>Repeated narrow test after the specified permission or loader fix</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="build-your-boundary-record"> <a href="#build-your-boundary-record" title="Build Your Boundary Record">Build Your Boundary Record</a> <a href="#build-your-boundary-record" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build Your Boundary Record">#</a> </h2> <p>Create a <strong>one-page assessment</strong> from the synthetic case or your prepared VM. Include exact object names and evidence references. Another reviewer should understand both the finding and its uncertainty without reproducing a risky action.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Current principal and token: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Controlled object and required operation: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Permission evidence and collection time: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Privileged consumer and version: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Actual path selection evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Approved trigger and recovery owner: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Claim established / claim still untested: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Minimal validation and stopping condition: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Remediation owner and retest evidence: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Completion standard:</strong> Distinguish configuration exposure from demonstrated execution, identify at least one invalidating condition, and choose a fix at the actual weak boundary. Tightening an unrelated directory does not repair the documented dependency.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Does querying a service prove modification rights?</strong></td> <td>No, querying and changing configuration require different access rights</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does a writable PATH entry prove hijacking?</strong></td> <td>No, establish actual search behavior, selection, privilege, and trigger</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which architecture matters for a DLL?</strong></td> <td>The loading process and its supported native module architecture</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which synthetic finding deserves more work?</strong></td> <td>B, because evidence connects controlled input to a privileged consumer</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does no callback prove no execution?</strong></td> <td>No, distinguish execution evidence from result transport and collection</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What makes remediation convincing?</strong></td> <td>A fix addressing the documented boundary plus a scoped retest</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Carry the <strong>permission-boundary record</strong> into <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 14: Privileged Persistence and Process Migration"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/privileged-persistence-and-process-migration/"> <a href="/red-team-course/privileged-persistence-and-process-migration/" rel="follow me" >Module 14: Privileged Persistence and Process Migration</a> </span> . The next lesson examines service state, process lifetime, and whether an additional persistence mechanism serves the mission objective.</p> <p>Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 14: Privileged Persistence and Process Migration
item.description: Understand Windows service persistence, process lifetime, architecture, and migration tradeoffs through read-only inspection and a service lifecycle exercise.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Privileged persistence</strong> preserves an approved execution opportunity across a defined interruption. A Windows service is one possible mechanism. Its configured account, startup behavior, running process, and recovery dependencies need separate verification.</p> <p>This module teaches you to build a <strong>service lifecycle record</strong> and judge whether process migration serves a concrete requirement. A running callback proves connectivity at one moment. It does not establish boot durability, service health, or successful restoration.</p> <p><em>Allow 35–45 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. The timeline exercise uses synthetic observations.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Distinguish</strong> service configuration, service state, and process lifetime.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> account selection and filesystem redirection.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> a prepared service without changing its configuration.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate</strong> migration against stability and evidence requirements.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a lifecycle record covering trigger, observation, and restoration.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>Use the <strong>prepared Windows lab VM</strong> and service manifest from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="local privilege escalation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/local-privilege-escalation/"> <a href="/red-team-course/local-privilege-escalation/" rel="follow me" >local privilege escalation</a> </span> . You need the exact training service name, expected executable path, permitted inspection account, and the owner’s expected start and stop behavior. An instructor-provided trace supports the paper exercise if no VM is available.</p> <p>The commands below are <strong>read-only queries</strong>. A separate service demonstration needs an approved benign service program, a bounded trigger, and a restoration plan. An arbitrary console executable is not a substitute for a program implementing the service interface.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Prerequisite</th> <th>Why it matters</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Service manifest</strong></td> <td>Separates lab-owned objects from operating-system services</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Baseline account</strong></td> <td>Establishes the identity expected during execution</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Lifecycle description</strong></td> <td>Defines whether the service stays running or completes a task</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Collection window</strong></td> <td>Connects configuration and process evidence in time</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery owner</strong></td> <td>Resolves failures before another experiment starts</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="separate-four-states"> <a href="#separate-four-states" title="Separate Four States">Separate Four States</a> <a href="#separate-four-states" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Four States">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Service configuration</strong> specifies properties such as executable path, startup mode, and account. <strong>Service state</strong> describes its current relationship with the Service Control Manager, or SCM. <strong>Process state</strong> describes a particular executing instance. <strong>Session state</strong> describes the operator’s connection or task transport.</p> <p>These states often change together, but they are <strong>not interchangeable</strong>. A service is configured even while stopped. A process might exit before an operator retrieves its result. A lost connection might leave a process running. Design observations around each state instead of using a callback as the single success signal.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Layer</th> <th>Example question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Configuration</strong></td> <td>What program and account should the service use?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Service state</strong></td> <td>Does SCM report running, stopped, or a pending transition?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Process state</strong></td> <td>Which process instance executed, and when did it exit?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Session state</strong></td> <td>Did the expected result reach the operator?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="follow-the-service-lifecycle"> <a href="#follow-the-service-lifecycle" title="Follow the Service Lifecycle">Follow the Service Lifecycle</a> <a href="#follow-the-service-lifecycle" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Follow the Service Lifecycle">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/service-process-session-lifecycle.webp", "caption": "Four panels distinguish service configuration, an approved start event, process evidence, and verified restoration after a Windows service exercise", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.70855802 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.266258341", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.70855802 +0000 UTC m=+499.266258341"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/service-process-session-lifecycle.webp" alt="Four panels distinguish service configuration, an approved start event, process evidence, and verified restoration after a Windows service exercise"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>A service result needs configuration, runtime, and restoration evidence</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p>A <strong>Windows service program</strong> implements SCM interfaces for startup and control handling. Services use different accounts and startup arrangements, and some share a process. A service is not inherently LocalSystem, automatically started, or a guarantee of durable access. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s service-program documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/services/service-programs"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/services/service-programs" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s service-program documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p>Your <strong>success condition</strong> follows the exercise objective. A one-shot maintenance service might legitimately stop after completing work. A continuously running service stopping unexpectedly is a different outcome. Record the program’s intended lifecycle before interpreting its state.</p> <blockquote> <p><strong>Key takeaway:</strong> A stopped service is a state to explain, not a universal success or failure signal.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="read-the-service-baseline"> <a href="#read-the-service-baseline" title="Read the Service Baseline">Read the Service Baseline</a> <a href="#read-the-service-baseline" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Read the Service Baseline">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>sc.exe qc CourseLabService </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sc.exe query CourseLabService </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>sc.exe qc</code></strong> reads configuration, while <strong><code>sc.exe query</code></strong> reports service state and related status fields. Record both outputs with timestamps. An error or missing service belongs in the result, and a similarly named service is not an acceptable substitute. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s configuration query"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/cc742055%28v%3Dws.11%29"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/cc742055%28v%3Dws.11%29" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s configuration query</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="state query"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/sc-query"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/sc-query" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >state query</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$service = Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Service ` </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -Filter <span style="color:#e6db74">"Name = 'CourseLabService'"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$service | Select-Object Name, State, StartMode, StartName, PathName, ProcessId </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>Win32_Service</code></strong> exposes the selected service’s state, configured account, path, startup mode, and process ID. The filter narrows the query to the named lab object. A zero or unavailable process ID does not name a running service process. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s Win32_Service class"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-service"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-service" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s Win32_Service class</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> ($null <span style="color:#f92672">-ne</span> $service <span style="color:#f92672">-and</span> $service.ProcessId <span style="color:#f92672">-gt</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">0</span>) { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Get-Process -Id $service.ProcessId -ErrorAction Stop | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Select-Object Id, ProcessName, StartTime, Path </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Process correlation</strong> is time-sensitive. A service might stop between the two queries, a PID might be reused, or access to a property might be denied. Preserve those limitations instead of inventing missing values. This example reads process properties through <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Get-Process"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/get-process?view=powershell-7.5"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/get-process?view=powershell-7.5" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Get-Process</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Expected result:</strong> A prepared running service supplies a service record and, with sufficient query access, a matching process observation. These commands were checked against documentation, not executed on the macOS authoring host. Your VM supplies the actual runtime evidence.</p> <h2 id="resolve-architecture-questions"> <a href="#resolve-architecture-questions" title="Resolve Architecture Questions">Resolve Architecture Questions</a> <a href="#resolve-architecture-questions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Resolve Architecture Questions">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Filesystem redirection</strong> affects some paths requested by 32-bit applications on 64-bit Windows. The <strong><code>Sysnative</code></strong> alias lets a 32-bit application address the native system directory. It is not a real directory or a universal path for every process. Microsoft also documents exceptions to redirection. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Windows filesystem redirector"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/file-system-redirector"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/file-system-redirector" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Windows filesystem redirector</a> </span> .</p> <p>Separate the <strong>querying process</strong>, the configured executable, and any library it loads. A 32-bit management process does not inherently require migration before inspecting or configuring a service. Verify the resolved path and the application’s compatibility instead of treating a change of process as a mandatory ritual.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Evidence to collect</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Which OS architecture?</strong></td> <td>Host inventory</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which process architecture?</strong></td> <td>Process properties for the relevant instance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which executable path?</strong></td> <td>Service configuration and file identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which path was used?</strong></td> <td>Runtime process or file-access evidence</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="evaluate-process-migration"> <a href="#evaluate-process-migration" title="Evaluate Process Migration">Evaluate Process Migration</a> <a href="#evaluate-process-migration" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Evaluate Process Migration">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Process migration</strong> places an agent’s execution into a different process context, depending on the tool’s implementation. It is distinct from changing a service’s stored configuration. Moving execution does not automatically preserve every task, handle, impersonation state, or communication property.</p> <p>Windows checks <strong>process access rights</strong> for operations such as querying information, writing process memory, and creating threads. Permissions and process protections constrain the available operations. A familiar executable name does not remove those boundaries. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s process security and access rights"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-security-and-access-rights"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-security-and-access-rights" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s process security and access rights</a> </span> .</p> <p>The right decision begins with the <strong>operational requirement</strong>. If a compatible approved process already satisfies the objective, another transition adds dependencies and cleanup work. If a lab investigates migration itself, define the expected before-and-after identity, architecture, task behavior, and failure result.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Consideration</th> <th>Review question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Lifetime</strong></td> <td>What event ends the destination process?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Compatibility</strong></td> <td>Does the implementation support the destination architecture?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Identity</strong></td> <td>Which primary or impersonation context applies afterward?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Stability</strong></td> <td>What legitimate function fails if the destination exits?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>Which source proves the transition occurred?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Restoration</strong></td> <td>Which processes and configuration changes remain afterward?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>No universal safe process list</strong> exists. A process’s role, protection, workload, and lifetime matter more than its basename. Avoid inferring either guaranteed detection or guaranteed concealment from names such as <strong><code>rundll32.exe</code></strong>.</p> <h2 id="observe-process-evidence"> <a href="#observe-process-evidence" title="Observe Process Evidence">Observe Process Evidence</a> <a href="#observe-process-evidence" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Observe Process Evidence">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Sysinternals: System Monitor deep dive (demo) | Sysmon, device, driver, Windows | Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/6W6pXp6EojY/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6W6pXp6EojY"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="6W6pXp6EojY" videotitle="Sysinternals: System Monitor deep dive (demo) | Sysmon, device, driver, Windows | Microsoft" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6W6pXp6EojY" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Sysinternals: System Monitor deep dive (demo) | Sysmon, device, driver, Windows | Microsoft"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Sysinternals: System Monitor deep dive (demo) | Sysmon, device, driver, Windows | Microsoft", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/6W6pXp6EojY\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6W6pXp6EojY", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Microsoft’s Sysmon demonstration</strong> provides context for observing endpoint behavior. While watching, distinguish a recorded event from a detection rule and an analyst’s conclusion. Collection configuration determines which event types are available. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6W6pXp6EojY"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6W6pXp6EojY" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <p>A <strong>service installation event</strong>, where the relevant auditing is enabled, records an installation rather than proving later service health or successful execution. Preserve service metadata and correlate it with the exercise timeline. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s event 4697 reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4697"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4697" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s event 4697 reference</a> </span> .</p> <p>For your <strong>collection plan</strong>, request only the events needed to answer the exercise question. A full host capture introduces review volume and potential sensitive data. An absent event needs a collection-health check before it becomes a statement about the tested behavior.</p> <h2 id="analyze-a-stopped-service"> <a href="#analyze-a-stopped-service" title="Analyze a Stopped Service">Analyze a Stopped Service</a> <a href="#analyze-a-stopped-service" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Analyze a Stopped Service">#</a> </h2> <p>This <strong>synthetic timeline</strong> describes an instructor’s one-shot service. The service manifest says it launches a benign worker and reports completion after dispatch. The worker writes a lab marker and exits independently.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Time</th> <th>Observation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>10:00:00</strong></td> <td>Approved start request accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>10:00:01</strong></td> <td>Service process and worker creation recorded</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>10:00:02</strong></td> <td>SCM reports the service stopped</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>10:00:03</strong></td> <td>Worker writes the expected marker</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>10:00:05</strong></td> <td>Worker exit recorded</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The <strong>supported conclusion</strong> is successful dispatch and worker completion for this specific fixture. The stopped state agrees with its documented design. A callback without the worker evidence would support a weaker conclusion, and the same timeline would violate a continuously running service’s expected behavior.</p> <p><strong>Durability remains untested.</strong> The timeline contains no reboot, dependency outage, or later trigger. If boot survival is the actual requirement, define a separate approved test. Do not use one successful start to claim resilience across events the exercise never observed.</p> <h2 id="plan-restoration-early"> <a href="#plan-restoration-early" title="Plan Restoration Early">Plan Restoration Early</a> <a href="#plan-restoration-early" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Plan Restoration Early">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>lifecycle record</strong> links each created object to its owner and original state. A newly created lab service and a modified pre-existing service require different restoration actions. Deleting a borrowed service would remove the customer’s original configuration.</p> <p>Service removal also has <strong>asynchronous consequences</strong>. Microsoft’s deletion API marks a service for deletion, and removal waits for relevant handles to close and the service to stop. A successful deletion request therefore needs a later verification. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="DeleteService behavior"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsvc/nf-winsvc-deleteservice"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsvc/nf-winsvc-deleteservice" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >DeleteService behavior</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Object</th> <th>Restoration question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Service registration</strong></td> <td>Was it created for the lab or present beforehand?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Configuration</strong></td> <td>Which exact fields changed from baseline?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Processes</strong></td> <td>Which lab-owned instances are still running?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Files</strong></td> <td>Which hashes and paths identify the lab’s files?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>Where are logs retained for the joint review?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="create-your-lifecycle-record"> <a href="#create-your-lifecycle-record" title="Create Your Lifecycle Record">Create Your Lifecycle Record</a> <a href="#create-your-lifecycle-record" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create Your Lifecycle Record">#</a> </h2> <p>Prepare a <strong>service lifecycle record</strong> for the synthetic timeline. Include one alternative explanation for a missing marker and one reason to avoid migration. Your review should establish the exercise outcome without assuming any unobserved startup behavior.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Service name and owner: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Original account, startup mode, and path: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Expected lifecycle and approved trigger: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Service and process observations with timestamps: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Identity and architecture evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Migration requirement or reason to omit it: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Observed result and untested durability condition: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Restoration action, owner, and verification: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> The one-shot fixture succeeded within its stated lifecycle, but boot persistence was not tested. Migration supplies no benefit to this short benign task unless the exercise explicitly studies a process transition. A missing marker needs execution and collection checks before attributing failure to SCM.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Does every service run as SYSTEM?</strong></td> <td>No, inspect the configured account and actual execution context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does stopped always mean success?</strong></td> <td>No, compare observed state with the program’s intended lifecycle</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does x86 management require migration?</strong></td> <td>No, investigate compatibility and path resolution directly</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Is a process basename a safety guarantee?</strong></td> <td>No, assess role, access rights, lifetime, and failure consequences</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does one start prove boot durability?</strong></td> <td>No, the boot condition needs its own approved observation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does deletion success finish cleanup?</strong></td> <td>No, verify final registration, runtime state, and owned artifacts</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Bring the <strong>lifecycle record</strong> to <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 15: Persistence Cleanup and Defense Evasion"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/persistence-cleanup-and-defense-evasion/"> <a href="/red-team-course/persistence-cleanup-and-defense-evasion/" rel="follow me" >Module 15: Persistence Cleanup and Defense Evasion</a> </span> . Use it to restore the exact objects touched by the exercise and preserve the evidence needed for a joint review.</p> <p>Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 15: Persistence Cleanup and Defense Evasion
item.description: Restore persistence changes with a precise artifact ledger, correct registry identity, evidence preservation, and independent verification of cleanup.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Cleanup restores agreed system state</strong> after an exercise. It removes or reverses the team’s changes while preserving the evidence needed to explain them. Deleting a visible file is only one possible step, and a failed query does not prove an artifact is absent.</p> <p>This module develops a <strong>restoration ledger</strong> linking ownership, baseline, action, verification, and unresolved work. It also separates defense-evasion testing from evidence destruction, so the assessment’s final state remains reviewable.</p> <p><em>Allow 30–45 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. The worked cleanup case uses synthetic records.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> restoration, artifact ownership, and verification scope.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> how registry identity and loaded hives affect cleanup.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> the exact Run entry from the earlier benign exercise.</li> <li><strong>Analyze</strong> failed queries, file identity changes, and remaining processes.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a restoration ledger with an independent review condition.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>Bring the <strong>baseline records</strong> from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="user persistence"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/user-persistence/"> <a href="/red-team-course/user-persistence/" rel="follow me" >user persistence</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="privileged persistence"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/privileged-persistence-and-process-migration/"> <a href="/red-team-course/privileged-persistence-and-process-migration/" rel="follow me" >privileged persistence</a> </span> . You need the original account SID, registry location and view, named values, owned files, process observations, and any configuration fields changed during the exercise.</p> <p>Use the <strong>same disposable VM</strong> for the inspection example. If you did not complete the Notepad Run-entry exercise, use the synthetic case instead. This lesson does not create another persistence mechanism or assume every reader has a matching artifact.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Input</th> <th>Why cleanup needs it</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Original state</strong></td> <td>Distinguishes restoration from deletion</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Ownership evidence</strong></td> <td>Prevents removing a similarly named customer object</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Exact identity</strong></td> <td>Selects the intended user’s configuration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Runtime record</strong></td> <td>Finds lab activity still running after trigger removal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence location</strong></td> <td>Preserves observations for the final report</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="define-the-restoration-target"> <a href="#define-the-restoration-target" title="Define the Restoration Target">Define the Restoration Target</a> <a href="#define-the-restoration-target" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Define the Restoration Target">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>created object</strong> usually needs removal if the exercise owns it and the agreement requires no residual artifact. A <strong>modified object</strong> needs restoration of the affected fields to the agreed baseline. An <strong>observed object</strong> needs no cleanup merely because it appeared in a tool’s output.</p> <p>For example, the earlier <strong>Notepad exercise</strong> created a named Run value, not the Windows Notepad application. Removing the lab value and closing its identified window addresses those changes. Deleting the operating-system executable would damage an unrelated component.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Object category</th> <th>Appropriate disposition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Created lab value</strong></td> <td>Remove the exact owned value after comparison</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Modified existing setting</strong></td> <td>Restore approved baseline fields</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Existing OS executable</strong></td> <td>Leave intact</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Collected evidence</strong></td> <td>Retain according to the engagement agreement</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Unrecognized change</strong></td> <td>Escalate for ownership review before mutation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="follow-the-restoration-loop"> <a href="#follow-the-restoration-loop" title="Follow the Restoration Loop">Follow the Restoration Loop</a> <a href="#follow-the-restoration-loop" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Follow the Restoration Loop">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/artifact-restoration-and-verification.webp", "caption": "A restoration loop connects artifact ownership and baseline, current-state comparison, selective restoration, and independent verification with retained evidence", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.713894203 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.271594524", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.713894203 +0000 UTC m=+499.271594524"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/artifact-restoration-and-verification.webp" alt="A restoration loop connects artifact ownership and baseline, current-state comparison, selective restoration, and independent verification with retained evidence"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>An action result and a verified final state are separate entries in the cleanup record</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p>The <strong>restoration loop</strong> begins with a comparison, not a deletion command. Confirm the current object still matches the team’s recorded change. Apply the narrow reversal, then independently check the intended final state and any affected trigger.</p> <p><strong>Concurrent changes</strong> complicate rollback. If an administrator edited a value after the exercise created it, blindly restoring an old snapshot might erase legitimate work. Record the mismatch, preserve the current value, and let the system owner resolve the conflict.</p> <blockquote> <p><strong>Decision rule:</strong> An uncertain owner or changed value is a review task, not permission for broader deletion.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="resolve-registry-identity"> <a href="#resolve-registry-identity" title="Resolve Registry Identity">Resolve Registry Identity</a> <a href="#resolve-registry-identity" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Resolve Registry Identity">#</a> </h2> <p><strong><code>HKCU</code></strong> refers to a current-user registry mapping. Its behavior follows process and security context, with caching details relevant to impersonating applications. A SYSTEM-context cleanup tool should not assume this handle refers to the interactive user who created the artifact. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s predefined registry keys"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/predefined-keys"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/predefined-keys" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s predefined registry keys</a> </span> .</p> <p>Use the <strong>recorded SID</strong> and account authority from the creation record. A short username alone is ambiguous across local and domain accounts. SID length does not distinguish a local account from a domain account, and a <strong><code>_Classes</code></strong> suffix identifies a different registry branch rather than an account’s domain status. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s security identifier documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/security-identifiers"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/security-identifiers" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s security identifier documentation</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Interpretation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>HKCU value absent</strong></td> <td>Absence in the queried mapping, if the query succeeded</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recorded SID under HKU</strong></td> <td>A loaded branch available for a targeted query</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recorded SID not listed</strong></td> <td>Investigate profile loading and collection context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Similar username</strong></td> <td>Insufficient evidence of the same security principal</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Loaded hives</strong> are not a complete user-account inventory. If the target profile is unloaded, a live HKU listing does not prove its persisted configuration is clean. Prefer verification in the original user’s controlled session, or an owner-managed profile inspection procedure with its own rollback plan.</p> <h2 id="inspect-the-exact-value"> <a href="#inspect-the-exact-value" title="Inspect the Exact Value">Inspect the Exact Value</a> <a href="#inspect-the-exact-value" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect the Exact Value">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>whoami.exe /user </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>reg.exe query HKU </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Identity inspection</strong> records the account executing cleanup and lists the loaded registry roots visible to it. Compare the result with the SID captured during the earlier exercise. Do not choose a SID by its position, length, or resemblance to a screenshot.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$recordedSid = <span style="color:#e6db74">'S-1-5-21-111111111-222222222-333333333-1001'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$runKey = <span style="color:#e6db74">"HKU\</span>$recordedSid<span style="color:#e6db74">\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>reg.exe query $runKey /v CourseLab-Notepad /reg<span style="color:#960050;background-color:#1e0010">:</span><span style="color:#ae81ff">64</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$queryExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$queryExitCode </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Replace the synthetic SID</strong> with the exact recorded SID before running the query. <strong><code>/v</code></strong> selects the lab value, and <strong><code>/reg:64</code></strong> matches the earlier exercise’s 64-bit registry view. <strong><code>$LASTEXITCODE</code></strong> preserves the native command’s exit result. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s reg query reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-query"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/reg-query" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s reg query reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Expected interpretation:</strong> A successful result reveals the named value and its current data. A failure requires the accompanying error text. Missing key, missing value, and access denied are different outcomes. This example is documentation-reviewed and requires a Windows lab for execution validation.</p> <p>For the <strong>actual removal</strong>, use the guarded, value-specific cleanup in <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 12"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/user-persistence/#verify-restoration-separately"> <a href="/red-team-course/user-persistence/#verify-restoration-separately" rel="follow me" >Module 12</a> </span> from the original user’s session. Compare the current name and data with the recorded lab value first. Do not delete the parent Run key, which contains other startup entries.</p> <h2 id="verify-file-ownership"> <a href="#verify-file-ownership" title="Verify File Ownership">Verify File Ownership</a> <a href="#verify-file-ownership" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify File Ownership">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-FileHash -LiteralPath <span style="color:#e6db74">'C:\CourseLab\Artifacts\example-marker.txt'</span> ` </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -Algorithm SHA256 </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>Get-FileHash</code></strong> reads file content to calculate a digest. Use this example only for a lab-owned file recorded in your manifest. The digest helps compare current content with the creation record, but a matching hash alone does not establish ownership or justify deletion. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s Get-FileHash documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/get-filehash?view=powershell-7.5"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/get-filehash?view=powershell-7.5" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s Get-FileHash documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p>Record the <strong>exact path, owner, and purpose</strong> alongside the digest. Two copies of the same lab file require two artifact records. A file containing another team’s data needs a different disposition even if its name resembles your test artifact.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Comparison</th> <th>Decision</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Path and digest match</strong></td> <td>Continue with the approved ownership-based reversal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Digest changed</strong></td> <td>Preserve and investigate the intervening change</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Path absent</strong></td> <td>Check query success and record the observation time</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Access denied</strong></td> <td>Diagnose access before drawing a content conclusion</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="diagnose-cleanup-failures"> <a href="#diagnose-cleanup-failures" title="Diagnose Cleanup Failures">Diagnose Cleanup Failures</a> <a href="#diagnose-cleanup-failures" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Diagnose Cleanup Failures">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Access denied</strong> does not prove a live agent is holding a file. Windows distinguishes access-denied errors from sharing violations, and other conditions affect file operations. Preserve the exact native error rather than replacing it with a guessed explanation. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Windows system error codes"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/system-error-codes--0-499-"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/system-error-codes--0-499-" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Windows system error codes</a> </span> .</p> <p>A <strong>remaining process</strong> requires its own ownership check. PID alone is insufficient after a long delay because identifiers are reused. Correlate image, start time, parent relationship, and the original exercise record before closing an application or asking the owner to stop a service.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Failure</th> <th>Narrow next check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Registry access denied</strong></td> <td>Query account, requested view, and object permissions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>File sharing violation</strong></td> <td>Identify the handle owner and expected application state</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Service marked for deletion</strong></td> <td>Check running state and outstanding management handles</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Artifact reappears</strong></td> <td>Look for another recorded trigger or management policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Process remains</strong></td> <td>Determine whether trigger removal affected an existing instance</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Trigger removal</strong> prevents a future launch through the removed mechanism. It does not automatically end existing activity or remove every alternate launch source. The final check should cover both the startup configuration and the known running lab instance.</p> <h2 id="observe-with-process-monitor"> <a href="#observe-with-process-monitor" title="Observe With Process Monitor">Observe With Process Monitor</a> <a href="#observe-with-process-monitor" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Observe With Process Monitor">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Sysinternals: Process Monitor deep dive (demo) | ProcMon, registry, process, Windows | Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/9H0Dz3NbNYQ/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9H0Dz3NbNYQ"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="9H0Dz3NbNYQ" videotitle="Sysinternals: Process Monitor deep dive (demo) | ProcMon, registry, process, Windows | Microsoft" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9H0Dz3NbNYQ" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Sysinternals: Process Monitor deep dive (demo) | ProcMon, registry, process, Windows | Microsoft"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Sysinternals: Process Monitor deep dive (demo) | ProcMon, registry, process, Windows | Microsoft", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/9H0Dz3NbNYQ\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9H0Dz3NbNYQ", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Microsoft’s Process Monitor demonstration</strong> supplements the file and registry investigation. Focus on process identity, operation, path, result, and event time. An unsuccessful lookup means something different from a successful write or delete. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9H0Dz3NbNYQ"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9H0Dz3NbNYQ" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Process Monitor</strong> collects filesystem, registry, and process/thread activity and supports filtering. Use a bounded collection window and preserve the original capture before narrowing the analyst view. Filters help review, but an incomplete capture does not establish the absence of an earlier operation. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s Process Monitor documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/procmon"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/procmon" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s Process Monitor documentation</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="preserve-detection-evidence"> <a href="#preserve-detection-evidence" title="Preserve Detection Evidence">Preserve Detection Evidence</a> <a href="#preserve-detection-evidence" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Preserve Detection Evidence">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Defense-evasion testing</strong> examines whether a defined change affects prevention or detection under specified conditions. Its result belongs beside the original configuration, exact test window, and collection status. Fewer child processes or a changed command line does not establish invisibility.</p> <p><strong>Assessment cleanup</strong> should preserve customer event logs and agreed evidence. If an exercise includes a defense-evasion hypothesis, document its measured outcome and restore any authorized configuration change. Do not relabel log destruction as routine housekeeping. Revisit <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="communication and detection comparisons"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/malleable-c2-and-communication-evasion/"> <a href="/red-team-course/malleable-c2-and-communication-evasion/" rel="follow me" >communication and detection comparisons</a> </span> for a controlled comparison method.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Record</th> <th>Preserve for review</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Endpoint observation</strong></td> <td>Raw event reference and collection status</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Operator action</strong></td> <td>Exact object, time, and task result</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Detection outcome</strong></td> <td>Alert, prevention action, or reviewed absence within a window</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Restoration result</strong></td> <td>Action status plus final-state verification</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="review-a-synthetic-cleanup"> <a href="#review-a-synthetic-cleanup" title="Review a Synthetic Cleanup">Review a Synthetic Cleanup</a> <a href="#review-a-synthetic-cleanup" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Review a Synthetic Cleanup">#</a> </h2> <p>Assume a <strong>training Run value</strong> was created for user A, and cleanup occurs later under an administrative account. The operator queries its own HKCU, receives no matching value, and marks cleanup complete. A later sign-in by user A opens the lab Notepad window again.</p> <p>The <strong>failure is scope</strong>, not a mysterious registry recovery. The operator queried a different mapping and never verified the original trigger.
