Correct the ledger to unresolved, return to the recorded SID and view, and compare the actual lab entry with its creation record.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence</th> <th>Supported conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Administrator’s HKCU lacks value</strong></td> <td>No matching value in the queried context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>User A’s entry still exists</strong></td> <td>The original trigger remains configured</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Known lab window launches later</strong></td> <td>Runtime behavior is consistent with incomplete cleanup</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Exact value removed and logon retested</strong></td> <td>Stronger evidence of restoration for this mechanism</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> Successful verification names the right account, value, view, and trigger. A remaining Notepad window from before removal does not prove a new launch. Close the identified lab instance before the controlled later sign-in and correlate new process evidence.</p> <h2 id="create-a-restoration-ledger"> <a href="#create-a-restoration-ledger" title="Create a Restoration Ledger">Create a Restoration Ledger</a> <a href="#create-a-restoration-ledger" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create a Restoration Ledger">#</a> </h2> <p>Build a <strong>ledger entry</strong> for the Run value and a second for any lab-owned file. Mark each as verified, unresolved, or retained by agreement. Avoid a single blanket “host clean” statement when the evidence covers only selected artifacts.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Host and artifact identifier: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Owning exercise and creation evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Original state / exercise change: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Current identity, location, view, and value: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Comparison result and conflicts: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Approved restoration action and result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Independent query and trigger verification: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Retained evidence and remaining work: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Reviewer, owner, and completion time: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Completion standard:</strong> Another reviewer should reproduce your final-state check without guessing the account or deleting additional objects. Unresolved items need an owner and next action, not an optimistic completion label.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>What if a pre-existing value was modified?</strong></td> <td>Restore its agreed baseline instead of deleting it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does an empty HKCU query prove cleanup?</strong></td> <td>Only for the verified queried context and successful query</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does SID length identify domain accounts?</strong></td> <td>No, use the recorded identifier and account authority</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does access denied prove a live implant?</strong></td> <td>No, inspect the exact error and object-access conditions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Why retest the trigger?</strong></td> <td>Configuration absence and future launch behavior are separate observations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What happens to customer logs?</strong></td> <td>Preserve them for the agreed review and retention process</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Carry the <strong>restoration ledger</strong> into <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 16: Domain Privilege Escalation and Kerberos Abuse"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/domain-privilege-escalation-and-kerberos-abuse/"> <a href="/red-team-course/domain-privilege-escalation-and-kerberos-abuse/" rel="follow me" >Module 16: Domain Privilege Escalation and Kerberos Abuse</a> </span> . The next lesson separates ticket requests, password exposure, and account authorization before evaluating domain impact.</p> <p>Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 16: Domain Privilege Escalation and Kerberos Abuse
item.description: Analyze Kerberos service-ticket exposure, account privilege, encryption choices, and delegation evidence with a domain escalation review record.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Domain privilege escalation</strong> combines identity, ticket, directory, and authorization evidence. Kerberoasting is one possible path. A service principal name (SPN) identifies a service account for Kerberos, but it does not grant administrative authority to the account.</p> <p>This module builds a <strong>ticket and privilege review</strong>. You will distinguish a ticket request from offline password analysis, compare service-account designs, and produce a defensible decision about the next approved test.</p> <p><em>Allow 40–55 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. Examples use synthetic account names and expected evidence.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> KDC, TGT, TGS, SPN, service account, and delegation.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> why ticket encryption and account privilege are separate questions.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> ticket-cache and directory evidence in an approved lab.</li> <li><strong>Compare</strong> traditional service accounts with managed service accounts.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a domain escalation review with evidence and limits.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>Use the <strong>domain lab and collection agreement</strong> from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="networking and Active Directory"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/foundations-networking-and-active-directory/"> <a href="/red-team-course/foundations-networking-and-active-directory/" rel="follow me" >networking and Active Directory</a> </span> . Record the requesting principal, domain controller, account names, SPNs, encryption types, and the purpose of each service. Do not request tickets for customer accounts outside the approved scope.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Record</th> <th>Why it matters</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Requesting identity</strong></td> <td>Attributes the ticket request to a real principal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Service account</strong></td> <td>Separates SPN ownership from authorization</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Encryption type</strong></td> <td>Determines which analysis paths are relevant</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Group membership</strong></td> <td>Establishes potential impact after authentication</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Collection window</strong></td> <td>Connects directory and controller evidence</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="map-kerberos-roles"> <a href="#map-kerberos-roles" title="Map Kerberos Roles">Map Kerberos Roles</a> <a href="#map-kerberos-roles" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Map Kerberos Roles">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/kerberos-ticket-exposure-and-impact.webp", "caption": "A Kerberos flow separates ticket request, encryption evidence, account authority, and service authorization", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.717897048 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.275597359", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.717897048 +0000 UTC m=+499.275597359"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/kerberos-ticket-exposure-and-impact.webp" alt="A Kerberos flow separates ticket request, encryption evidence, account authority, and service authorization"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Ticket exposure and account impact require separate evidence</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p><strong>Kerberos</strong> uses a key distribution center (KDC) to issue tickets. A <strong>ticket-granting ticket (TGT)</strong> represents an authenticated session. A <strong>ticket-granting service ticket (TGS)</strong> authorizes access to a named service and is issued for an SPN.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Component</th> <th>Role</th> <th>Does it prove privilege?</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>KDC</strong></td> <td>Issues tickets for the domain</td> <td>No</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TGT</strong></td> <td>Requests later service tickets</td> <td>No</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TGS</strong></td> <td>Targets one service SPN</td> <td>No</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>SPN</strong></td> <td>Maps a service name to an account</td> <td>No</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Group membership</strong></td> <td>Contributes to authorization</td> <td>Sometimes, after policy evaluation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>An SPN is a <strong>directory mapping</strong>, not an access-control decision. A service account might have no elevated groups, or it might run a critical application with delegated rights. Review both the account and the service it supports.</p> <h2 id="separate-request-and-crack"> <a href="#separate-request-and-crack" title="Separate Request and Crack">Separate Request and Crack</a> <a href="#separate-request-and-crack" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Request and Crack">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Kerberoasting</strong> describes requesting service tickets for SPN-associated accounts and analyzing the ticket material offline. The KDC request is a network event. The password-guessing phase runs against a captured representation and does not contact the KDC for each guess.</p> <p>An <strong>offline result is uncertain</strong>. Long random passwords, AES keys, account rotation, and managed service accounts change the feasibility of guessing. A failed guess does not prove the account is safe, while a recovered password still requires an authorization review before any use.</p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Kerberos Deep Dive Part 2 - Kerberoasting"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/PhNspeJ0r-4/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PhNspeJ0r-4"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="PhNspeJ0r-4" videotitle="Kerberos Deep Dive Part 2 - Kerberoasting" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PhNspeJ0r-4" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Kerberos Deep Dive Part 2 - Kerberoasting"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Kerberos Deep Dive Part 2 - Kerberoasting", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/PhNspeJ0r-4\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PhNspeJ0r-4", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Compass Security’s Kerberos presentation</strong> supplements the ticket flow. Track which claims describe protocol behavior and which depend on an account’s password, groups, or delegation settings. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch the presentation on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PhNspeJ0r-4"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PhNspeJ0r-4" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch the presentation on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="review-encryption-evidence"> <a href="#review-encryption-evidence" title="Review Encryption Evidence">Review Encryption Evidence</a> <a href="#review-encryption-evidence" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Review Encryption Evidence">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>RC4-HMAC</strong> and <strong>AES</strong> are different Kerberos encryption choices. Hashcat mode 13100 is commonly associated with Kerberoastable RC4 ticket material. It is not a universal mode for every ticket representation or encryption type. Confirm the format and encryption field before selecting an analysis method.</p> <p>Event 4769 records a <strong>Kerberos service-ticket request</strong> on a domain controller when auditing is enabled. Current Windows documentation includes fields for the requesting account, service name, ticket encryption type, client address, and status. The event shows a request, not a password crack or successful service use. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s event 4769 reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4769"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4769" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s event 4769 reference</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence</th> <th>Supports</th> <th>Does not support</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>4769 success</strong></td> <td>A TGS request reached the KDC</td> <td>Password recovery</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>RC4 encryption field</strong></td> <td>RC4-specific review path</td> <td>Weak password by itself</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Offline candidate</strong></td> <td>A possible secret match</td> <td>Authorization to use it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Privileged group member</strong></td> <td>Potential high impact</td> <td>Current session access</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="compare-account-designs"> <a href="#compare-account-designs" title="Compare Account Designs">Compare Account Designs</a> <a href="#compare-account-designs" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare Account Designs">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Traditional user service accounts</strong> often keep long-lived secrets managed by a team. <strong>Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSAs)</strong> allow Windows to manage password retrieval and rotation for approved hosts. Neither design removes the need to review SPNs, delegation, groups, or service scope. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s gMSA overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/group-managed-service-accounts/group-managed-service-accounts/group-managed-service-accounts-overview"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/group-managed-service-accounts/group-managed-service-accounts/group-managed-service-accounts-overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s gMSA overview</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Design</th> <th>Secret management</th> <th>Review focus</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Traditional account</strong></td> <td>Team-managed password and rotation</td> <td>Age, length, reuse, and owner</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>gMSA</strong></td> <td>Directory-managed rotation</td> <td>Allowed hosts and delegated use</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Computer account</strong></td> <td>Machine-managed secret</td> <td>SPNs, delegation, and machine role</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Disabled account</strong></td> <td>Authentication disabled</td> <td>Stale SPNs and ownership cleanup</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>SPN ownership</strong> also needs review. Duplicate SPNs, stale registrations, and undocumented services create confusing ticket evidence. Resolve the directory object and application owner before assigning impact.</p> <h2 id="examine-delegation-carefully"> <a href="#examine-delegation-carefully" title="Examine Delegation Carefully">Examine Delegation Carefully</a> <a href="#examine-delegation-carefully" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Examine Delegation Carefully">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Delegation</strong> permits one service or computer to act toward another service under defined conditions. Unconstrained, constrained, and resource-based constrained delegation use different directory attributes and trust assumptions. A delegation flag alone does not identify which users or services are impersonated in the observed scenario.</p> <p>Use the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="MITRE ATT&CK Kerberoasting reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/003/"> <a href="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/003/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >MITRE ATT&CK Kerberoasting reference</a> </span> </strong> as a taxonomy aid, then validate the actual domain configuration. Record the relevant attribute, object owner, allowed principals, target service, and time of observation. Avoid treating a technique label as evidence of successful abuse.</p> <h2 id="inspect-a-lab-ticket-cache"> <a href="#inspect-a-lab-ticket-cache" title="Inspect a Lab Ticket Cache">Inspect a Lab Ticket Cache</a> <a href="#inspect-a-lab-ticket-cache" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect a Lab Ticket Cache">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>klist.exe </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>klist.exe get cifs/fileserver.corp.example </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>klist.exe</code></strong> displays and requests tickets for the current logon session. Use the second command only against the named lab service and within the approved window. Preserve the output without publishing ticket blobs or secrets. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s klist reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/klist"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/klist" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s klist reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Expected result:</strong> The lab either shows a TGS for the requested SPN or returns an error because the service, DNS record, or policy is unavailable. Either result needs the requesting identity, target SPN, time, and controller evidence. This command was documentation-reviewed and not executed on the macOS authoring host.</p> <h2 id="analyze-a-synthetic-case"> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-case" title="Analyze a Synthetic Case">Analyze a Synthetic Case</a> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-case" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Analyze a Synthetic Case">#</a> </h2> <p>Assume <strong>analyst.user</strong> requests a TGS for <code>HTTP/reporting.corp.example</code>. Event 4769 records success with AES encryption. The service account is a gMSA allowed on two application hosts and has no privileged group membership. No offline candidate matches the captured lab fixture.</p> <p>The <strong>defensible conclusion</strong> is a successful service-ticket request for a managed account. The evidence does not show password recovery, domain privilege, or unauthorized service use. A follow-up should review the gMSA host scope and SPN ownership rather than escalate the severity solely because a ticket exists.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Correct interpretation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Ticket request</strong></td> <td>KDC issued or attempted a TGS</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>AES type</strong></td> <td>Encryption choice recorded in the event</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>gMSA owner</strong></td> <td>Rotation and host policy apply</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No password match</strong></td> <td>Offline test did not recover the lab secret</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No privileged group</strong></td> <td>No group-based domain-admin claim</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="choose-the-next-test"> <a href="#choose-the-next-test" title="Choose the Next Test">Choose the Next Test</a> <a href="#choose-the-next-test" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose the Next Test">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>bounded next test</strong> should resolve one uncertainty. If the question is SPN ownership, query directory metadata. If it is ticket monitoring, correlate event 4769 with the requesting host. If it is service authorization, inspect the application’s access control. Do not combine password analysis, delegation changes, and remote access in one unexplained action.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Uncertainty</th> <th>Smallest useful evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Who owns the SPN?</strong></td> <td>Directory object and owner record</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which encryption was used?</strong></td> <td>Event 4769 encryption field</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Account resource reachability</strong></td> <td>Approved authorization test</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Did a password guess succeed?</strong></td> <td>Reproducible lab fixture result</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="create-the-review-record"> <a href="#create-the-review-record" title="Create the Review Record">Create the Review Record</a> <a href="#create-the-review-record" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Review Record">#</a> </h2> <p>Produce a <strong>ticket and privilege review</strong> for the synthetic case. Include the request event, account design, group and delegation evidence, offline result, and one condition able to change your conclusion.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Requesting principal and host: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Domain controller and event reference: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Target SPN and owning object: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Ticket type and encryption evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Account design, groups, and delegation: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Offline analysis scope and result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Authorization impact established / untested: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Next approved observation and stopping condition: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Owner, timestamp, and retention location: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Completion standard:</strong> A reviewer sees which fact came from the KDC, directory, endpoint, or offline analysis. The record states what remains untested.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Does an SPN grant admin rights?</strong></td> <td>No, it maps a service name to an account</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What does event 4769 show?</strong></td> <td>A service-ticket request on the domain controller</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does RC4 prove a weak password?</strong></td> <td>No, it identifies an encryption path for review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does a recovered secret prove authorization?</strong></td> <td>No, groups, ACLs, and policy still determine access</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Why review gMSAs separately?</strong></td> <td>Their managed rotation and host scope alter exposure</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What makes a conclusion defensible?</strong></td> <td>Source-specific evidence plus explicit untested conditions</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Carry the <strong>ticket and privilege review</strong> into <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 17: Lateral Movement and Expanding Access"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/lateral-movement-and-expanding-access/"> <a href="/red-team-course/lateral-movement-and-expanding-access/" rel="follow me" >Module 17: Lateral Movement and Expanding Access</a> </span> . The next module uses it to test path prerequisites without assuming every credential reaches every host.</p> <p>Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 17: Lateral Movement and Expanding Access
item.description: Plan lateral movement with explicit name resolution, authentication, authorization, service, and rollback evidence instead of assuming every credential reaches every host.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Lateral movement</strong> is a sequence of host-to-host decisions. A credential, route, protocol, service, and authorization rule each influence the result. One successful login does not prove access to every server or every administrative function.</p> <p>This module creates a <strong>movement path ledger</strong>. You will separate network reachability, authentication, authorization, execution, and result collection so a failed attempt produces useful evidence.</p> <p><em>Allow 35–50 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. The examples use an approved lab inventory.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> reachability, authentication, authorization, and execution.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> why a valid credential does not imply remote administration.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> a named host and service using read-only checks.</li> <li><strong>Compare</strong> SMB, WinRM, and SSH prerequisites.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a path ledger with a stopping condition.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use the host and identity records</strong> from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="domain privilege escalation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/domain-privilege-escalation-and-kerberos-abuse/"> <a href="/red-team-course/domain-privilege-escalation-and-kerberos-abuse/" rel="follow me" >domain privilege escalation</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="host operations"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/situational-awareness-and-host-operations/"> <a href="/red-team-course/situational-awareness-and-host-operations/" rel="follow me" >host operations</a> </span> . The lab manifest should list source host, destination host, approved protocol, account, time window, and owner. Do not scan or authenticate to unlisted hosts.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Gate</th> <th>Evidence to collect</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Name resolution</strong></td> <td>Resolved address and resolver used</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Network path</strong></td> <td>Route, port, and firewall result</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Authentication</strong></td> <td>Protocol response and account identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Authorization</strong></td> <td>Requested action and access decision</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution</strong></td> <td>Process or service evidence on destination</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Collection</strong></td> <td>Returned output and timestamp</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="model-the-five-gates"> <a href="#model-the-five-gates" title="Model the Five Gates">Model the Five Gates</a> <a href="#model-the-five-gates" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Model the Five Gates">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/movement-gates-and-path-ledger.webp", "caption": "A movement path passes through name resolution, transport, authentication, authorization, execution, and collection gates", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.721160238 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.278860559", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.721160238 +0000 UTC m=+499.278860559"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/movement-gates-and-path-ledger.webp" alt="A movement path passes through name resolution, transport, authentication, authorization, execution, and collection gates"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>A path ledger keeps each remote-access gate visible</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p><strong>Reachability</strong> asks whether packets are able to reach a service. <strong>Authentication</strong> asks whether the endpoint accepts the presented identity. <strong>Authorization</strong> asks whether the identity is permitted to perform the requested operation. <strong>Execution</strong> asks whether the operation created the intended remote activity. <strong>Collection</strong> asks whether the result returned to the operator.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Gate</th> <th>Failure example</th> <th>Correct conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Reachability</strong></td> <td>Port blocked</td> <td>No transport path observed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Authentication</strong></td> <td>Logon rejected</td> <td>Credential or protocol failure, not bad DNS by itself</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Authorization</strong></td> <td>Access denied</td> <td>Identity reached the service but lacks which right</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution</strong></td> <td>Service did not start</td> <td>Remote action outcome is unproven</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Collection</strong></td> <td>Session timed out</td> <td>Result transport is unproven</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Treating all five as “access” hides the next useful test. A <strong>valid password</strong> still fails because the account is denied network logon, the service is disabled, or the requested operation needs a separate right.</p> <h2 id="name-the-destination-precisely"> <a href="#name-the-destination-precisely" title="Name the Destination Precisely">Name the Destination Precisely</a> <a href="#name-the-destination-precisely" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Name the Destination Precisely">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Resolve-DnsName fileserver.corp.example </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Test-NetConnection fileserver.corp.example -Port <span style="color:#ae81ff">445</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>Resolve-DnsName</code></strong> records the answer returned by the selected resolver. <strong><code>Test-NetConnection</code></strong> tests a TCP path to the named port. Neither command authenticates or authorizes an action. Preserve address, port, interface, and time in the ledger.</p> <p><strong>Expected result:</strong> The lab might return multiple addresses, a failed lookup, or a closed port. A DNS answer does not prove the endpoint is the intended host, and an open port does not prove a successful logon. These commands were documentation-reviewed and not executed on the macOS authoring host.</p> <h2 id="compare-remote-services"> <a href="#compare-remote-services" title="Compare Remote Services">Compare Remote Services</a> <a href="#compare-remote-services" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare Remote Services">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>SMB</strong> commonly supports file and named-pipe access. <strong>WinRM</strong> exposes Windows management through configured HTTP or HTTPS listeners and policy. <strong>SSH</strong> supports password, key, certificate, or GSSAPI methods depending on server configuration. Each protocol has its own authorization model and audit trail.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Service</th> <th>Reachability</th> <th>Authorization question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>SMB</strong></td> <td>TCP 445 and server policy</td> <td>Share and filesystem rights</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>WinRM</strong></td> <td>Listener and firewall policy</td> <td>Remote-management group and endpoint policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>SSH</strong></td> <td>Listener and host policy</td> <td>Allowed account, key, shell, and command policy</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Do not infer</strong> an HTTPS page implies WinRM, or an open SMB port grants administrative shares. Confirm the protocol and resource named in the exercise.</p> <h2 id="track-error-meaning"> <a href="#track-error-meaning" title="Track Error Meaning">Track Error Meaning</a> <a href="#track-error-meaning" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Track Error Meaning">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Error 1326</strong> commonly maps to a logon failure, but the surrounding protocol and account policy still matter. A path-not-found response might reflect an incorrect share, route, or name. DNS, authentication, authorization, and resource errors need their original text and protocol context.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Symptom</th> <th>First review</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Name not resolved</strong></td> <td>Resolver, suffix, and manifest spelling</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Port closed</strong></td> <td>Destination service state and firewall owner</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Logon failure</strong></td> <td>Account, method, time, and policy response</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Access denied</strong></td> <td>Requested resource and effective rights</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Path not found</strong></td> <td>Share name, namespace, and server response</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Timeout</strong></td> <td>Transport, service, and result-collection windows</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-a-movement-demonstration"> <a href="#watch-a-movement-demonstration" title="Watch a Movement Demonstration">Watch a Movement Demonstration</a> <a href="#watch-a-movement-demonstration" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch a Movement Demonstration">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Sysinternals: PsTools deep dive (demo) | Command line tool, remote management, Windows | Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/XWq3v9Z6pgo/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XWq3v9Z6pgo"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="XWq3v9Z6pgo" videotitle="Sysinternals: PsTools deep dive (demo) | Command line tool, remote management, Windows | Microsoft" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XWq3v9Z6pgo" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Sysinternals: PsTools deep dive (demo) | Command line tool, remote management, Windows | Microsoft"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Sysinternals: PsTools deep dive (demo) | Command line tool, remote management, Windows | Microsoft", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/XWq3v9Z6pgo\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XWq3v9Z6pgo", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Microsoft’s PsTools demonstration</strong> shows remote administration utilities and their operational context. Use it to identify which actions require remote service access and which produce process or service evidence. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch the demonstration on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XWq3v9Z6pgo"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XWq3v9Z6pgo" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch the demonstration on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <p>**The video is a supplement, It does not prove every lab account uses every tool. Record the selected tool, destination, requested operation, and resulting event before assigning impact.</p> <h2 id="build-a-movement-path"> <a href="#build-a-movement-path" title="Build a Movement Path">Build a Movement Path</a> <a href="#build-a-movement-path" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build a Movement Path">#</a> </h2> <p>Start with the <strong>least expansive action</strong> answering the question. A read-only share listing might resolve resource ownership. A remote service query might confirm configuration. A command changing state needs a separate approval and rollback entry.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Source host and principal: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Destination host and owner: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Name and address evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Protocol, port, and listener evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Authentication method and result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Requested resource or operation: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Authorization result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Execution and collection evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Rollback owner and stopping condition: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Path completeness</strong> matters. If the destination process ran but no output returned, report execution and collection separately. If authentication succeeded but the share denied access, report authentication without claiming file access.</p> <h2 id="analyze-a-synthetic-failure"> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-failure" title="Analyze a Synthetic Failure">Analyze a Synthetic Failure</a> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-failure" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Analyze a Synthetic Failure">#</a> </h2> <p>Assume <strong>analyst.user</strong> resolves <code>app01.corp.example</code> to <code>10.20.30.14</code>. TCP 5985 is open. WinRM accepts the account, but the endpoint denies the requested command because the user is not in the approved remote-management group.</p> <p>The <strong>supported conclusion</strong> is name resolution, transport, and authentication success. Authorization and execution failed. The next action is an owner-approved group or endpoint-policy review, not a second protocol chosen at random.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence</th> <th>Claim supported</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>DNS answer</strong></td> <td>Name resolved at the recorded time</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Open 5985</strong></td> <td>TCP path to the listener exists</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>WinRM logon</strong></td> <td>Endpoint accepted the identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Endpoint denial</strong></td> <td>Requested operation was not authorized</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No process event</strong></td> <td>No execution evidence in the collected window</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="evaluate-expansion-risk"> <a href="#evaluate-expansion-risk" title="Evaluate Expansion Risk">Evaluate Expansion Risk</a> <a href="#evaluate-expansion-risk" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Evaluate Expansion Risk">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Expanding access</strong> increases the number of hosts, accounts, and owners affected by the exercise. A broad credential sweep creates more audit events and more cleanup obligations. Limit each move to the host and operation answering the mission question.</p> <p>Consider <strong>credential scope</strong>, <strong>host criticality</strong>, <strong>service impact</strong>, and <strong>evidence quality</strong> before proceeding. A destination appearing reachable might be a production controller, a backup server, or a safety-critical system. The asset owner and engagement scope determine whether the test is appropriate.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Decision factor</th> <th>Question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Need</strong></td> <td>Does this host answer the objective?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Exposure</strong></td> <td>Which account and data cross the boundary?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Impact</strong></td> <td>Would the action interrupt a service?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>What exact result will prove or disprove the hypothesis?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Who restores state if the action fails?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="create-the-path-ledger"> <a href="#create-the-path-ledger" title="Create the Path Ledger">Create the Path Ledger</a> <a href="#create-the-path-ledger" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Path Ledger">#</a> </h2> <p>Produce a <strong>movement path ledger</strong> for the synthetic WinRM case and one proposed SMB comparison. Include the gate which failed, an alternative explanation, and the smallest owner-approved next check.</p> <p><strong>Completion standard:</strong> A reviewer distinguishes a network result, an authentication result, an authorization result, and an execution result. The ledger contains no claim based only on a port scan or credential possession.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Does an open port prove remote execution?</strong></td> <td>No, it proves only a transport path to a listener</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does successful authentication prove share access?</strong></td> <td>No, resource authorization is a separate gate</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What does error context add?</strong></td> <td>It distinguishes protocol, resource, and policy failures</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Why avoid broad credential sweeps?</strong></td> <td>They add scope, telemetry, and cleanup without proving the objective</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What should follow an endpoint denial?</strong></td> <td>An owner-approved policy or group review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What makes the ledger complete?</strong></td> <td>Evidence for each gate plus an explicit stopping condition</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Carry the <strong>movement path ledger</strong> into <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 18: Cross-Domain Pivoting and LDAP Enumeration"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/cross-domain-pivoting-and-ldap-enumeration/"> <a href="/red-team-course/cross-domain-pivoting-and-ldap-enumeration/" rel="follow me" >Module 18: Cross-Domain Pivoting and LDAP Enumeration</a> </span> , where trust direction and directory query scope add more gates.</p> <p>Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 18: Cross-Domain Pivoting and LDAP Enumeration
item.description: Analyze trust direction, selective authentication, SID filtering, LDAP scope, and query results with a cross-domain pivot decision record.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Cross-domain pivoting</strong> depends on trust direction, name resolution, authentication, authorization, and directory visibility. A trust does not make every object readable or every credential valid in both domains.</p> <p>This module creates a <strong>trust and query record</strong>. You will identify the queried directory, constrain LDAP filters, and decide whether a proposed cross-domain action has enough evidence to proceed.</p> <p><em>Allow 35–50 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. The examples are synthetic and read-only.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> trust direction, LDAP, DN, SID filtering, and selective authentication.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> why a trust relationship does not imply broad access.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> a bounded LDAP query and its server scope.</li> <li><strong>Compare</strong> query visibility with authorization to act.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a trust and query decision record.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>**Bring the source and destination records from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="lateral movement"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/lateral-movement-and-expanding-access/"> <a href="/red-team-course/lateral-movement-and-expanding-access/" rel="follow me" >lateral movement</a> </span> . Record the source principal’s domain, target domain, resolver, domain controller, approved query base, and owner. Cross-domain queries need explicit scope because directory data includes sensitive identities and group relationships.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Field</th> <th>Record</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Source domain</strong></td> <td>Domain and account authority</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Target domain</strong></td> <td>Domain and directory owner</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Trust direction</strong></td> <td>Direction from the queried relationship</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Authentication</strong></td> <td>Account and protocol used</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>LDAP base</strong></td> <td>Exact naming context and organizational unit</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Filter and limit</strong></td> <td>Object classes, attributes, and page size</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="read-trust-direction"> <a href="#read-trust-direction" title="Read Trust Direction">Read Trust Direction</a> <a href="#read-trust-direction" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Read Trust Direction">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>trust direction</strong> is relative to the two named domains. If domain A trusts domain B, accounts from B might be accepted by A under configured conditions. The phrase does not describe every reverse operation, resource ACL, or group membership.</p> <p><strong>Selective authentication</strong> requires explicit permission to authenticate to particular computers. <strong>SID filtering</strong> limits how security identifiers from a trusted domain are interpreted across the boundary. Forest and external trusts also differ in scope and transitivity. Validate the actual trust object and policy rather than relying on a diagram label.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Does not establish</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Trust exists</strong></td> <td>Universal resource access</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Direction is outbound</strong></td> <td>Reverse trust</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Name resolves</strong></td> <td>Authentication or authorization</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Authentication succeeds</strong></td> <td>LDAP read or group membership</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Object is visible</strong></td> <td>Permission to change it</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="define-ldap-scope"> <a href="#define-ldap-scope" title="Define LDAP Scope">Define LDAP Scope</a> <a href="#define-ldap-scope" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Define LDAP Scope">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/trust-direction-and-ldap-scope.webp", "caption": "Two domains connect through a directional trust while LDAP base, filter, authorization, and host access remain separate boundaries", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.723982442 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.281682754", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.723982442 +0000 UTC m=+499.281682754"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/trust-direction-and-ldap-scope.webp" alt="Two domains connect through a directional trust while LDAP base, filter, authorization, and host access remain separate boundaries"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Trust direction and query scope constrain a cross-domain pivot</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p><strong>LDAP</strong> is a directory protocol. A <strong>distinguished name (DN)</strong> identifies an object location, while a server name identifies where the query is sent. A valid DN on one server does not prove the same object exists in another directory.</p> <p><strong>Object classes matter.</strong> In Active Directory, a filter for <code>objectClass=user</code> includes user and computer objects because computer objects inherit from user-related classes. Use explicit attributes and classes when the exercise needs human accounts.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Query choice</th> <th>Risk to review</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Base DN</strong></td> <td>Querying the wrong naming context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Filter</strong></td> <td>Returning computers or service objects unintentionally</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Attributes</strong></td> <td>Collecting more identity data than needed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Paging</strong></td> <td>Missing or duplicating results across pages</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Escaping</strong></td> <td>Altering filter meaning with special characters</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="run-a-bounded-query"> <a href="#run-a-bounded-query" title="Run a Bounded Query">Run a Bounded Query</a> <a href="#run-a-bounded-query" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Run a Bounded Query">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$base = <span style="color:#e6db74">"DC=target,DC=corp,DC=example"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$filter = <span style="color:#e6db74">"(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user)(sAMAccountName=analyst.user))"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADUser -Server <span style="color:#e6db74">"dc01.target.corp.example"</span> -SearchBase $base ` </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -LDAPFilter $filter -Properties memberOf,servicePrincipalName </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>-Server</code></strong> names the directory endpoint. <strong><code>-SearchBase</code></strong> limits the naming context, and the filter selects a person user with an exact account name. <strong><code>-Properties</code></strong> requests only the attributes needed for the review. This command requires the ActiveDirectory module and an approved lab account. It was documentation-reviewed, not executed on the macOS authoring host.</p> <p><strong>Expected result:</strong> The lab might return one user, no user, or an access error. A result needs server, base, filter, attributes, page behavior, and timestamp. Do not infer a trust or authorization decision from an empty result without checking query scope and collection health.</p> <h2 id="watch-directory-context"> <a href="#watch-directory-context" title="Watch Directory Context">Watch Directory Context</a> <a href="#watch-directory-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch Directory Context">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Kerberos Deep Dive Part 1 - Introduction"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/pzrtfRpPVM4/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzrtfRpPVM4"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="pzrtfRpPVM4" videotitle="Kerberos Deep Dive Part 1 - Introduction" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzrtfRpPVM4" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Kerberos Deep Dive Part 1 - Introduction"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Kerberos Deep Dive Part 1 - Introduction", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/pzrtfRpPVM4\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzrtfRpPVM4", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Compass Security’s Kerberos introduction</strong> supplies protocol context for cross-domain authentication. Use it to distinguish domain tickets from LDAP authorization and to note where trust policy enters the flow. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch the presentation on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzrtfRpPVM4"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzrtfRpPVM4" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch the presentation on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>The presentation is supplemental.</strong> Record your domain’s actual trust objects, supported encryption types, and authorization policy before making a claim.</p> <h2 id="analyze-a-synthetic-trust"> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-trust" title="Analyze a Synthetic Trust">Analyze a Synthetic Trust</a> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-trust" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Analyze a Synthetic Trust">#</a> </h2> <p>Assume <strong>source.corp.example</strong> has a one-way trust to <strong>target.corp.example</strong>. The source user resolves a target controller and authenticates, but LDAP search returns access denied for the requested organizational unit. Selective authentication is enabled for target servers.</p> <p>The <strong>supported conclusion</strong> states DNS and an authentication exchange reached the target. Directory authorization for the search base failed. The trust’s existence does not prove broad LDAP visibility or access to target hosts.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence</th> <th>Supported claim</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Target controller resolved</strong></td> <td>Name resolution succeeded</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Authentication accepted</strong></td> <td>The protocol accepted the principal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>LDAP access denied</strong></td> <td>The requested directory read was not authorized</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Selective authentication</strong></td> <td>Computer-specific permission needs review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No group result</strong></td> <td>Group membership remains unobserved</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="choose-a-pivot-decision"> <a href="#choose-a-pivot-decision" title="Choose a Pivot Decision">Choose a Pivot Decision</a> <a href="#choose-a-pivot-decision" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose a Pivot Decision">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>pivot decision</strong> should state the target object, operation, principal, trust evidence, and stopping condition. If the goal is inventory, a narrow directory read might suffice. If the goal is remote administration, host logon rights and resource ACLs need separate proof.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Objective</th> <th>Next bounded check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Confirm trust</strong></td> <td>Read the named trust object and direction</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Confirm identity</strong></td> <td>Correlate authentication event and principal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Confirm LDAP scope</strong></td> <td>Repeat the exact base and filter with owner approval</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Confirm host access</strong></td> <td>Test the named host and operation, not a domain sweep</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Confirm privilege</strong></td> <td>Resolve group nesting and resource ACLs</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="create-the-trust-record"> <a href="#create-the-trust-record" title="Create the Trust Record">Create the Trust Record</a> <a href="#create-the-trust-record" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Trust Record">#</a> </h2> <p>Produce a <strong>trust and query decision record</strong> for the synthetic case. Include one alternative explanation for the access denial, the exact LDAP scope, and the evidence needed before a host pivot.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Source principal and domain: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Target domain, controller, and trust direction: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Selective-authentication or SID-filtering evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>LDAP base, filter, attributes, and page limit: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Authentication result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Directory authorization result: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Proposed host operation and owner: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Alternative explanation and next bounded test: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Stopping condition and evidence location: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Completion standard:</strong> The record identifies the directory queried and avoids converting object visibility into permission to modify or administer it.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Does a one-way trust work both ways?</strong></td> <td>No, direction is relative to the named domains</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does a valid DN prove a server connection?</strong></td> <td>No, server and naming context are separate</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does <code>objectClass=user</code> include computers?</strong></td> <td>Yes, use a more precise filter when needed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does LDAP visibility grant write access?</strong></td> <td>No, read and change rights are separate</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What does selective authentication change?</strong></td> <td>It adds explicit computer or resource authorization checks</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What makes a query reproducible?</strong></td> <td>Server, base, filter, attributes, limits, and timestamp</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Carry the <strong>trust and query record</strong> into <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 19: Fortifying Access and Operator Discipline"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/fortifying-access-and-operator-discipline/"> <a href="/red-team-course/fortifying-access-and-operator-discipline/" rel="follow me" >Module 19: Fortifying Access and Operator Discipline</a> </span> . The next module turns these boundaries into expiry, failover, and least-privilege decisions.</p> <p>Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 19: Fortifying Access and Operator Discipline
item.description: Design bounded red-team access with expiry, ownership, redundancy, failover, and operator records that remain useful during a live assessment.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Fortifying access</strong> means making the assessment reliable without expanding privilege or hiding uncontrolled dependencies. Longer polling intervals, multiple channels, or a trusted account do not automatically make operations safe or invisible.</p> <p>This module creates an <strong>access and failover plan</strong>. You will map dependencies, choose least-privilege access, define expiry, and evaluate a failure without claiming redundancy unsupported by the evidence.</p> <p><em>Allow 30–45 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. The plan uses a synthetic mission environment.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> least privilege, dependency, expiry, and failover.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> why redundancy shares a common failure.</li> <li><strong>Compare</strong> access designs by scope, owner, and recovery cost.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate</strong> an access change against the mission objective.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a bounded access and failover plan.</li> </ul> <h2 id="start-with-the-objective"> <a href="#start-with-the-objective" title="Start With the Objective">Start With the Objective</a> <a href="#start-with-the-objective" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Start With the Objective">#</a> </h2> <p>An <strong>access decision</strong> begins with the mission question. If the objective is to validate a single web control, a broad domain credential adds risk without adding evidence. If the objective requires a scheduled callback, the owner needs an expiry and recovery plan before any channel is enabled.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Smallest access candidate</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Read one application</strong></td> <td>Named account and application role</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Inspect one host</strong></td> <td>Time-limited management path</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Validate a domain control</strong></td> <td>Approved lab identity and controller</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Observe a scheduled task</strong></td> <td>Owner-approved task and window</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="map-shared-dependencies"> <a href="#map-shared-dependencies" title="Map Shared Dependencies">Map Shared Dependencies</a> <a href="#map-shared-dependencies" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Map Shared Dependencies">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/bounded-access-and-failover.webp", "caption": "An access plan connects a named owner and expiry to primary and independent fallback paths with shared dependencies marked", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.726213981 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.283914302", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.726213981 +0000 UTC m=+499.283914302"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/bounded-access-and-failover.webp" alt="An access plan connects a named owner and expiry to primary and independent fallback paths with shared dependencies marked"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Failover is useful only when its dependencies are genuinely independent</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p><strong>Redundancy</strong> fails when supposedly separate paths share DNS, credentials, cloud control planes, certificates, or a single operator device. Draw dependencies before adding a second channel. A longer beacon interval changes traffic frequency, not the visibility or reliability of the whole system.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Dependency</th> <th>Failure it shares</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>DNS provider</strong></td> <td>Name resolution outage</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Credential store</strong></td> <td>Account lockout or secret loss</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Certificate authority</strong></td> <td>TLS identity failure</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Cloud control plane</strong></td> <td>Provider or tenant outage</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Operator workstation</strong></td> <td>Local access and evidence loss</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Fallback</strong> should be a tested alternative with an owner, trigger, and recovery step.
