A second hostname on the same provider is a different route in configuration, but it is not independent infrastructure.</p> <h2 id="set-expiry-and-ownership"> <a href="#set-expiry-and-ownership" title="Set Expiry and Ownership">Set Expiry and Ownership</a> <a href="#set-expiry-and-ownership" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Set Expiry and Ownership">#</a> </h2> <p>Each <strong>credential, certificate, route, and scheduled action</strong> needs an owner and an end time. Record who revokes it, how revocation is verified, and what happens if the engagement ends early. Avoid shared credentials when a named account or role meets the objective.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Field</th> <th>Example decision</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Owner</strong></td> <td>Customer identity team</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Scope</strong></td> <td>One lab host and one operation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Start</strong></td> <td>Approved maintenance window</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Expiry</strong></td> <td>End of window plus review buffer</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Revocation</strong></td> <td>Disable account and verify access failure</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>Ticket, event record, and owner sign-off</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-a-defensive-context"> <a href="#watch-a-defensive-context" title="Watch a Defensive Context">Watch a Defensive Context</a> <a href="#watch-a-defensive-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch a Defensive Context">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Compass Security Beer-Talk: Purple Teaming - Verteidigung maximieren (17.09.2020, German)"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/xsfO8idEmBM/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsfO8idEmBM"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="xsfO8idEmBM" videotitle="Compass Security Beer-Talk: Purple Teaming - Verteidigung maximieren (17.09.2020, German)" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsfO8idEmBM" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Compass Security Beer-Talk: Purple Teaming - Verteidigung maximieren (17.09.2020, German)"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Compass Security Beer-Talk: Purple Teaming - Verteidigung maximieren (17.09.2020, German)", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/xsfO8idEmBM\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsfO8idEmBM", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Compass Security’s purple-team presentation</strong> adds context for coordinating offensive observations with defensive owners. Use it to ask which telemetry, escalation path, and decision record a live exercise needs. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch the presentation on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsfO8idEmBM"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsfO8idEmBM" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch the presentation on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <p>**The video does not replace the engagement rules. Your plan should identify the actual customer owner, evidence location, and approval boundary.</p> <h2 id="evaluate-a-channel-choice"> <a href="#evaluate-a-channel-choice" title="Evaluate a Channel Choice">Evaluate a Channel Choice</a> <a href="#evaluate-a-channel-choice" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Evaluate a Channel Choice">#</a> </h2> <p>Compare access designs by <strong>need</strong>, <strong>scope</strong>, <strong>dependency</strong>, <strong>telemetry</strong>, and <strong>recovery</strong>. A channel with fewer packets might still use a sensitive identity or leave a long-lived credential. A redundant channel might add more accounts and more revocation work.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Design</th> <th>Strength</th> <th>Trade-off</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Single named path</strong></td> <td>Simple ownership and rollback</td> <td>One dependency stops work</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Two independent paths</strong></td> <td>Better continuity</td> <td>More access and evidence to manage</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Shared emergency account</strong></td> <td>Quick handoff</td> <td>Weak attribution and revocation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Expiring role</strong></td> <td>Clear scope and owner</td> <td>Needs tested renewal process</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Justify the smallest design</strong> answering the objective. Add a second path only when its independent dependency and recovery value are documented.</p> <h2 id="work-a-failure-case"> <a href="#work-a-failure-case" title="Work a Failure Case">Work a Failure Case</a> <a href="#work-a-failure-case" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Work a Failure Case">#</a> </h2> <p>**Assume the primary control path uses <code>ops.corp.example</code> and a named assessment account. A second hostname points to the same provider and uses the same account. The provider has an outage during the approved window.</p> <p>The <strong>correct analysis</strong> is a shared dependency failure. Changing the hostname does not supply the missing provider or credential. The next action is the documented out-of-band contact or an owner-approved independent path, not an improvised account or channel.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Supported conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Two hostnames</strong></td> <td>Two configured names</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Same provider</strong></td> <td>Shared infrastructure dependency</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Same account</strong></td> <td>Shared credential dependency</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Provider outage</strong></td> <td>Both paths might fail</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Emergency account request</strong></td> <td>New access needs owner approval</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="create-the-access-plan"> <a href="#create-the-access-plan" title="Create the Access Plan">Create the Access Plan</a> <a href="#create-the-access-plan" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Access Plan">#</a> </h2> <p>Produce an <strong>access and failover plan</strong> for the failure case. Include the primary path, independent dependency, expiry, revocation, evidence, and a rule for stopping when no approved path remains.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Mission objective: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Primary identity, route, and owner: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Shared dependencies: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Independent fallback and its owner: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Start, expiry, and revocation checks: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Expected telemetry and review location: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Failure trigger and approved next action: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Stopping condition: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Completion standard:</strong> Another operator uses the plan without inventing credentials, scope, or recovery actions. The plan states when work stops.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Does a longer interval make access invisible?</strong></td> <td>No, it changes timing while other telemetry remains</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Are two hostnames independent?</strong></td> <td>Only if their provider, identity, and route dependencies differ</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Why name an owner?</strong></td> <td>Revocation and failure decisions need authority</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What makes least privilege practical?</strong></td> <td>A named operation, resource, time window, and review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>When should an operator stop?</strong></td> <td>When no approved path or recovery action remains</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What proves revocation?</strong></td> <td>Owner action plus a scoped access-failure check</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Carry the <strong>access and failover plan</strong> into <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 20: Mission Objectives and Reporting"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/mission-objectives-and-reporting/"> <a href="/red-team-course/mission-objectives-and-reporting/" rel="follow me" >Module 20: Mission Objectives and Reporting</a> </span> . The final module turns the plan, evidence, and limits into a report another team uses.</p> <p>Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 2: Mission Preparation and Infrastructure
item.description: Everything required before an attack: scope and rules of engagement, deconfliction, hardening the attack platform, standing up redirectors, and validating the infrastructure before go.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Mission preparation</strong> makes an assessment reproducible and controllable before the first test action. Scope, contacts, infrastructure ownership, evidence storage, and teardown belong in the same plan. This module turns the methodology test card into an operational readiness record.</p> <p><em>Allow 25 minutes for reading and 30 minutes for a preparation review. Complete Module 1 and use your own isolated lab for technical checks.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define scope:</strong> name approved assets, accounts, actions, and time windows.</li> <li><strong>Explain dependencies:</strong> separate the management path, assessment traffic, and evidence storage.</li> <li><strong>Inspect readiness:</strong> verify the paths the test depends on without assuming a webpage proves everything works.</li> <li><strong>Resolve uncertainty:</strong> pause for a recorded decision when a dependency or target is ambiguous.</li> <li><strong>Create an asset register:</strong> account for ownership, expiration, collection, and removal.</li> </ul> <h2 id="scope-is-more-than-addresses"> <a href="#scope-is-more-than-addresses" title="Scope Is More Than Addresses">Scope Is More Than Addresses</a> <a href="#scope-is-more-than-addresses" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Scope Is More Than Addresses">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>An address list</strong> is only one part of scope. An approved IP might host several tenants, a public hostname might point to a shared provider, and a login might expose both permitted and excluded resources. Record the relevant identities and actions as well as network locations.</p> <p><strong>Rules of engagement (ROE)</strong> describe how the assessment is conducted. The document should connect the objective, permitted work, exclusions, contacts, and response to unexpected events. NIST provides a rules-of-engagement template and assessment-planning guidance. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="NIST SP 800-115"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/115/final"> <a href="https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/115/final" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >NIST SP 800-115</a> </span> </p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Boundary</th> <th>Example entry</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Assets</strong></td> <td>Named lab hosts and an application tenant identifier</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Identities</strong></td> <td>Two designated synthetic accounts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Actions</strong></td> <td>Approved discovery and one sample-file permission test</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Time</strong></td> <td>Explicit start, pause, and end times with a time zone</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Exclusions</strong></td> <td>Production customer data and unrelated tenants</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Limits</strong></td> <td>Maximum requests, data volume, and permitted configuration changes</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Asset ownership and authorization are separate facts.</strong> A registration record, DNS response, or customer brand on a page is insufficient to establish permission to test the underlying service. Record any required provider or tenant authorization through the agreed engagement process.</p> <h2 id="make-stop-conditions-operational"> <a href="#make-stop-conditions-operational" title="Make Stop Conditions Operational">Make Stop Conditions Operational</a> <a href="#make-stop-conditions-operational" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Make Stop Conditions Operational">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A stop condition</strong> names an observable event and an immediate response. “Be careful” is not a useful instruction. “Pause if the sample query returns a real customer record, preserve the minimal incident reference, and contact the controller” is specific enough for another operator to follow.</p> <p><strong>A restart decision</strong> also needs an owner. After a pause, document what changed, who approved resumption, and which actions remain permitted. A timed outage window expiring does not silently renew itself.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Trigger</th> <th>Immediate action</th> <th>Decision owner</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Unexpected production data</strong></td> <td>Stop collection and preserve the minimal reference</td> <td>Exercise controller</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Service health degrades</strong></td> <td>Pause the action and record timestamps</td> <td>Service owner and controller</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Unrecognized callback or host</strong></td> <td>Stop interaction pending scope verification</td> <td>Controller</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Customer reports an incident</strong></td> <td>Compare records through the deconfliction channel</td> <td>Incident lead</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Deconfliction should work during an outage.</strong> Test a backup contact path which does not depend on the same application or network under assessment. Record who is able to stop work when the primary controller is unavailable.</p> <h2 id="separate-infrastructure-roles"> <a href="#separate-infrastructure-roles" title="Separate Infrastructure Roles">Separate Infrastructure Roles</a> <a href="#separate-infrastructure-roles" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Infrastructure Roles">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>The operator workstation</strong> is the management endpoint. A <strong>team server</strong> coordinates the assessment platform when one is used. A <strong>redirector</strong> forwards an approved traffic path, while an <strong>evidence store</strong> retains the records required for analysis and reporting. Some labs combine roles, but their permissions and failure dependencies still differ.</p> <p><strong>A redirector is not a guarantee of anonymity.</strong> Hosting, DNS, certificates, network logs, and server administration produce records. Its placement should follow the authorized test architecture and the customer’s expected observation points.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/engagement-infrastructure-responsibilities.webp", "caption": "Diagram separating operator management, assessment infrastructure, approved target systems, and controlled evidence storage", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.731321254 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.289021585", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.731321254 +0000 UTC m=+499.289021585"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/engagement-infrastructure-responsibilities.webp" alt="Diagram separating operator management, assessment infrastructure, approved target systems, and controlled evidence storage"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Map ownership and allowed communication for every assessment component</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Role</th> <th>Required inventory detail</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Operator endpoint</strong></td> <td>Responsible operator, authentication, and approved management access</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Assessment server</strong></td> <td>Owner, version, listeners, and retention settings</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Redirector</strong></td> <td>Domain, address, forwarding purpose, and expiration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence store</strong></td> <td>Access list, encryption, retention, and deletion owner</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Target dependency</strong></td> <td>Service owner, test boundary, and restoration contact</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Choose the smallest sufficient topology.</strong> A second approved path helps only if it addresses a real dependency and has its own cleanup plan. Two hosts on one provider, account, or network still share failure conditions. Redundancy is a design decision, not a fixed required number of servers.</p> <h2 id="build-a-lab-redirector"> <a href="#build-a-lab-redirector" title="Build a Lab Redirector">Build a Lab Redirector</a> <a href="#build-a-lab-redirector" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build a Lab Redirector">#</a> </h2> <p>Create the redirector as a <strong>small public edge VM</strong> in the customer-approved cloud account or provider account. Keep it separate from the operator workstation, assessment server, and target network. Select a region and jurisdiction approved by the engagement owner. A nearby region reduces avoidable latency, while provider reputation, data handling, and ownership matter more than a particular country.</p> <p><strong>The redirector should have one public address and one narrowly defined upstream path.</strong> Put the assessment server behind a private tunnel or an allowlisted origin address. Do not place the redirector inside the customer production network, give it a broad internal route, or reuse it as the evidence store. Those choices turn a forwarding host into an unnecessary bridge.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Placement decision</th> <th>Recommended lab choice</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Public edge</strong></td> <td>Separate low-cost VM in the approved provider account</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Origin</strong></td> <td>Assessment server on a private tunnel or fixed allowlist</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Management</strong></td> <td>Provider console or restricted admin source, separate from test traffic</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Ingress</strong></td> <td>TCP 80/443 only when the test requires them</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Egress</strong></td> <td>Origin address and approved update or monitoring services</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Expiration</strong></td> <td>Provider, address, domain, certificate, and VM teardown dates</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>For a benign HTTP exercise, install <strong>Nginx</strong> on the edge VM and proxy one named test path to a harmless origin service. The configuration below is a template for a disposable lab. Replace the example names and address with values in the connection matrix.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo apt update </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo apt install nginx </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo install -d -m <span style="color:#ae81ff">0750</span> /etc/nginx/lab </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudoedit /etc/nginx/sites-available/lab-redirector </span></span></code></pre></div><div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-nginx" data-lang="nginx"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">server</span> { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">listen</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">80</span>; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">server_name</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">redirector.lab.example</span>; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">access_log</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">/var/log/nginx/lab-redirector.access.log</span>; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">error_log</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">/var/log/nginx/lab-redirector.error.log</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">warn</span>; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">location</span> = <span style="color:#e6db74">/healthz</span> { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">add_header</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">Content-Type</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">text/plain</span>; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">return</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">200</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"lab</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">redirector</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">ready\n"</span>; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">location</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">/lab/</span> { </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">proxy_pass</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">http://10.30.0.10:8080</span>; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">proxy_set_header</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">Host</span> $host; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">proxy_set_header</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">X-Request-ID</span> $request_id; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">proxy_set_header</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">X-Forwarded-For</span> $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>} </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Enable the single site, check the syntax, and reload only after the configuration review:</strong></p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/lab-redirector /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/lab-redirector </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo nginx -t </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo systemctl reload nginx </span></span></code></pre></div><p>The origin address <strong>must be reachable from the redirector through the approved path</strong>. An RFC 1918 address in <code>proxy_pass</code> requires a private tunnel or a routed lab network. It does not create connectivity by itself. The origin should expose only the harmless test service and accept traffic from the redirector’s fixed address.</p> <p><strong>Test each leg with a unique request identifier.</strong> First query the edge health endpoint, then request the lab path, and finally compare the edge and origin logs. Do not use a payload, credential collector, or unrestricted forward rule for this readiness test.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl --fail http://redirector.lab.example/healthz </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl --fail -H <span style="color:#e6db74">'X-Lab-Request: prep-001'</span> http://redirector.lab.example/lab/healthz </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo journalctl -u nginx --since <span style="color:#e6db74">'5 minutes ago'</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Expected result:</strong> The health endpoint returns the fixed readiness text. The second request appears in the edge access log and the origin log with the same test identifier. A successful edge response without an origin record indicates a configuration, route, or collection problem. These commands are documentation examples for an authorized lab.</p> <p><strong>For HTTPS, use a certificate whose name matches the approved test domain</strong> and record its issuer, renewal owner, and expiry. Keep certificate automation separate from the test path. Validate TLS from the same client class used by the exercise, then preserve the certificate and access-log references in the readiness register. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Nginx proxy module documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html"> <a href="https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Nginx proxy module documentation</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Backout for the redirector</strong> is part of the build. Remove the enabled site, reload Nginx, revoke or delete the test certificate, remove the DNS record, destroy the VM, and verify the provider account has no remaining address, firewall rule, snapshot, or access key. Retain the agreed logs and teardown evidence instead of deleting the assessment record.</p> <h2 id="protect-management-and-evidence"> <a href="#protect-management-and-evidence" title="Protect Management and Evidence">Protect Management and Evidence</a> <a href="#protect-management-and-evidence" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Protect Management and Evidence">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Management access</strong> should expose only the services and sources needed by the assessment team. Define inbound and outbound requirements independently. A rule permitting all traffic from a broad customer subnet is different from a narrowly scoped management rule.</p> <p><strong>Protect the records as well as the listener.</strong> Assessment data includes credentials, screenshots, transcripts, and customer configuration. Restrict access to the people who need it, keep secrets out of command histories and shared notes, and document a retention deadline. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="NIST assessment data-handling guidance"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication800-115.pdf"> <a href="https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication800-115.pdf" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >NIST assessment data-handling guidance</a> </span> </p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Control</th> <th>Readiness question</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Authentication</strong></td> <td>Does each operator have accountable access?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Network policy</strong></td> <td>Are necessary sources, destinations, ports, and address families explicit?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Host updates</strong></td> <td>Are the selected versions and relevant maintenance decisions recorded?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Secret storage</strong></td> <td>Are operational secrets separated from general documentation?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence access</strong></td> <td>Is the reviewer able to read the required records without broad administrative access?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Is a known recovery path available before firewall or service changes?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Do not apply an incomplete firewall snippet remotely.</strong> A copied default-drop sequence often omits established connections, loopback, management recovery, IPv6, or required infrastructure traffic. Review the actual policy against a connection matrix and test it from a recoverable lab console.</p> <h2 id="inspect-listening-services"> <a href="#inspect-listening-services" title="Inspect Listening Services">Inspect Listening Services</a> <a href="#inspect-listening-services" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect Listening Services">#</a> </h2> <p>On your <strong>Linux assessment server</strong>, inspect current listeners and nftables policy without changing either:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo ss -lntup </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sudo nft list ruleset </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>ss</code></strong> reports socket information. <strong><code>-l</code></strong> selects listeners, <strong><code>-n</code></strong> keeps numeric addresses, <strong><code>-t</code></strong> and <strong><code>-u</code></strong> include TCP and UDP, and <strong><code>-p</code></strong> requests process information. Permissions affect which process details appear. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="ss manual"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ss.8.html"> <a href="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ss.8.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >ss manual</a> </span> </p> <p><strong><code>nft list ruleset</code></strong> displays nftables configuration. Interpret an empty output in the context of the host’s actual firewall stack and any provider firewall. A host-level ruleset alone does not describe every control on the network path. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Netfilter ruleset-management documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://wiki.nftables.org/wiki-nftables/index.php/Operations_at_ruleset_level"> <a href="https://wiki.nftables.org/wiki-nftables/index.php/Operations_at_ruleset_level" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Netfilter ruleset-management documentation</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Expected exercise result:</strong> Every listening socket has a documented purpose and owner. An unexpected listener is a finding to explain before launch, not something to terminate blindly. Compare the output with the connection matrix and preserve the timestamp.</p> <h2 id="verify-each-connection-leg"> <a href="#verify-each-connection-leg" title="Verify Each Connection Leg">Verify Each Connection Leg</a> <a href="#verify-each-connection-leg" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Each Connection Leg">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A browsable HTTPS endpoint</strong> establishes only the behavior of the request you sent. It does not establish the management path, an internal forwarding rule, the intended application exchange, or evidence collection. Test the intended path in a closed range using harmless test traffic.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Leg</th> <th>Check</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Name resolution</strong></td> <td>Resolve the approved domain through the intended resolver</td> <td>Name, address, resolver, and time</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TLS endpoint</strong></td> <td>Check the certificate and successful negotiation</td> <td>Hostname, validity, and observed endpoint</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Forwarded request</strong></td> <td>Send the designated harmless lab request</td> <td>Matching ingress and application records</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Management path</strong></td> <td>Authenticate through the approved operator route</td> <td>Operator identity and access log</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence collection</strong></td> <td>Locate the test record in the chosen store</td> <td>Record identifier and collection time</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Correlation beats assumption.</strong> Give the harmless test request a unique lab identifier and follow it through the expected logs. If the public endpoint succeeds but the downstream record is absent, investigate forwarding or collection before treating the entire path as ready.</p> <h2 id="domains-certificates-and-mail"> <a href="#domains-certificates-and-mail" title="Domains, Certificates, and Mail">Domains, Certificates, and Mail</a> <a href="#domains-certificates-and-mail" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Domains, Certificates, and Mail">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A TLS certificate</strong> supports authentication of the endpoint named in the certificate under the client’s trust rules. It does not certify the purpose or authorization of an assessment. Domain categorization also does not guarantee a filtering product permits traffic. Verify actual policy behavior in the approved test conditions.</p> <p><strong>A mail exercise</strong> needs a separate delivery plan. Record the sending service, approved recipients, expected message handling, and reporting channel. Begin with an inert message and a synthetic destination so routing and attribution are checked before the campaign-specific work in Module 10.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Item</th> <th>What to record</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Domain</strong></td> <td>Registrant or responsible owner, purpose, and expiration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Certificate</strong></td> <td>Subject names, issuer, validity, and renewal owner</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Mail sender</strong></td> <td>Account, sending service, authentication, and permitted recipients</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Delivery test</strong></td> <td>Message identifier, expected route, and observed result</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Teardown</strong></td> <td>Required revocation, removal, and evidence of completion</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Reputation is not a substitute for measurement.</strong> A newly registered domain being blocked is a meaningful observation about the tested policy. Whether the test should continue through another route depends on the objective and a recorded controller decision.</p> <h2 id="supplemental-video"> <a href="#supplemental-video" title="Supplemental Video">Supplemental Video</a> <a href="#supplemental-video" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Supplemental Video">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Micro Emulation Plans: Making Adversary Emulation Accessible"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/X4VuzccCDTU/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X4VuzccCDTU"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="X4VuzccCDTU" videotitle="Micro Emulation Plans: Making Adversary Emulation Accessible" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X4VuzccCDTU" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Micro Emulation Plans: Making Adversary Emulation Accessible"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Micro Emulation Plans: Making Adversary Emulation Accessible", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/X4VuzccCDTU\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X4VuzccCDTU", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Watch:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Micro Emulation Plans: Making Adversary Emulation Accessible"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X4VuzccCDTU"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X4VuzccCDTU" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Micro Emulation Plans: Making Adversary Emulation Accessible</a> </span> , published by SANS Offensive Operations and featured by the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://ctid.mitre.org/videos/micro-emulation-plans/"> <a href="https://ctid.mitre.org/videos/micro-emulation-plans/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense</a> </span> . Use the discussion of bounded tests to identify which infrastructure a particular objective needs.</p> <p><strong>Viewing task:</strong> Choose one proposed test and list its required identities, hosts, network paths, and observations. Remove components which do not support the test. Explain the remaining dependencies and how the operator would recognize a failed prerequisite.</p> <h2 id="rehearse-deconfliction"> <a href="#rehearse-deconfliction" title="Rehearse Deconfliction">Rehearse Deconfliction</a> <a href="#rehearse-deconfliction" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Rehearse Deconfliction">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Tabletop scenario:</strong> At 14:20 UTC, the customer reports an unexpected connection from an address assigned to the exercise. Your notes contain a different destination and a test completed ten minutes earlier. The address is shared by two approved operators.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> The shared source is insufficient attribution. Compare the destination, time, account, process or request identifier, and each operator’s record. Pause relevant activity while the incident lead determines whether the event belongs to the assessment. Do not label unmatched activity as yours to simplify the conversation.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Exercise and action ID: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Time, time zone, and known clock offset: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Operator and approved source: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Target asset and account context: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Intended action and expected effect: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Observed result and evidence reference: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Unexpected behavior: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Pause/resume decision and owner: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Review the rehearsal</strong> by checking whether another operator reconstructs the sequence from the record alone. Missing timestamps or shared anonymous access make the record less useful. Correct those gaps before the launch decision.</p> <h2 id="create-the-readiness-register"> <a href="#create-the-readiness-register" title="Create the Readiness Register">Create the Readiness Register</a> <a href="#create-the-readiness-register" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Readiness Register">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Build one row per asset</strong> using the template below. Include temporary domains, provider accounts, test identities, storage locations, and any persistent assessment component. An artifact absent from the register is easy to miss during teardown.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Asset identifier and purpose: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Owner and approved operator: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Address / domain / tenant / host: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Required inbound and outbound paths: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Authentication and secret location: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Evidence and retention location: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Expiration or removal deadline: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Recovery and teardown procedure: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Verification result and reviewer: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Go/no-go exercise:</strong> Your listeners are reachable, but the backup contact has not been tested and the evidence store rejects writes. Decide whether the operational prerequisites are satisfied. Separate technical connectivity from the ability to control and document the assessment.</p> <p><strong>Expected answer:</strong> The launch criteria are incomplete. Fix the failed evidence path, test the contact path, and record the verification. A functional connection alone does not satisfy the preparation requirements.</p> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Retain the readiness register</strong> alongside the Module 1 test card. Continue with <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 3: Networking and Active Directory Foundations"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/foundations-networking-and-active-directory/"> <a href="/red-team-course/foundations-networking-and-active-directory/" rel="follow me" >Module 3: Networking and Active Directory Foundations</a> </span> </strong> to interpret the connections and identities the plan depends on. Return to the <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >course hub</a> </span> </strong> for the complete sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 20: Mission Objectives and Reporting
item.description: Turn red-team objectives into bounded tests and evidence-backed findings with explicit limits, remediation owners, and retest conditions.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>A red-team report is a decision record.</strong> It links an approved objective to observed evidence, impact, limits, remediation ownership, and a retest condition. A dramatic technique name without those links does not help the customer choose a fix.</p> <p>This module creates a <strong>mission finding package</strong>. You will write a bounded objective, separate expected from observed behavior, and design a retest another assessor will reproduce.</p> <p><em>Allow 35–50 minutes. Difficulty: intermediate. The report example is synthetic.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> objective, observation, impact, limitation, and retest.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> why protocol support does not prove a configured access path.</li> <li><strong>Apply</strong> an evidence chain to a host or identity finding.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate</strong> competing explanations and remediation choices.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a concise finding package with an owner and retest.</li> </ul> <h2 id="start-with-the-objective"> <a href="#start-with-the-objective" title="Start With the Objective">Start With the Objective</a> <a href="#start-with-the-objective" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Start With the Objective">#</a> </h2> <p>An <strong>objective</strong> names the decision the assessment must inform. “Compromise the network” is too broad. “Determine whether the approved service account reads the reporting share from the staging host during the maintenance window” is testable.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Objective field</th> <th>Example</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Question</strong></td> <td>Does the account read the named share?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Source</strong></td> <td>Staging host and recorded principal</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Target</strong></td> <td>Reporting share on the approved server</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Window</strong></td> <td>2026-09-17 20:00–20:30 UTC</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Success evidence</strong></td> <td>Server-side access record and controlled file result</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Stop condition</strong></td> <td>No further access after first validated result</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="separate-expected-and-observed"> <a href="#separate-expected-and-observed" title="Separate Expected and Observed">Separate Expected and Observed</a> <a href="#separate-expected-and-observed" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Expected and Observed">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Expected behavior</strong> comes from documentation, a lab fixture, or a hypothesis. <strong>Observed behavior</strong> comes from a timestamped command, event, trace, or owner confirmation. A report should label the difference so a reader does not confuse a planned step with a completed action.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Statement</th> <th>Classification</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>SSH supports keys and certificates</strong></td> <td>Protocol capability</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>This server allows this key</strong></td> <td>Configuration observation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>A Linux host joined the AD domain</strong></td> <td>Environment observation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Plaintext credentials were collected</strong></td> <td>Evidence claim requiring a specific source</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Event 4624 occurred</strong></td> <td>Logon event, not physical user presence</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>SSH supports several authentication methods</strong> when configured. A Linux host joins an Active Directory domain, yet neither fact proves a stolen password, an interactive user, or administrative access. State the configured method and evidence source.</p> <h2 id="build-the-evidence-chain"> <a href="#build-the-evidence-chain" title="Build the Evidence Chain">Build the Evidence Chain</a> <a href="#build-the-evidence-chain" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build the Evidence Chain">#</a> </h2> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/objective-evidence-remediation-retest.webp", "caption": "A reporting flow connects a bounded objective to observed evidence, impact limits, remediation ownership, and a repeatable retest", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-09-23 04:19:53.733687445 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b499.291387756", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-23 04:19:53.733687445 +0000 UTC m=+499.291387756"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/objective-evidence-remediation-retest.webp" alt="A reporting flow connects a bounded objective to observed evidence, impact limits, remediation ownership, and a repeatable retest"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>A useful finding preserves the path from question to retest</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <p>An <strong>evidence chain</strong> has five links: objective, action, observation, interpretation, and decision. If a link is missing, reduce the claim. A failed collection step belongs in the limitation field rather than being silently treated as a negative result.</p> <p><strong>Impact</strong> should be concrete. Name the account, resource, data class, or control affected. Avoid universal claims such as “full domain compromise” unless the evidence in practice establishes the required authority and path.</p> <h2 id="watch-a-reporting-context"> <a href="#watch-a-reporting-context" title="Watch a Reporting Context">Watch a Reporting Context</a> <a href="#watch-a-reporting-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch a Reporting Context">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Compass Security Beer-Talk: Responding to Cyber Attacks"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/cULyBdtE-SM/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cULyBdtE-SM"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="cULyBdtE-SM" videotitle="Compass Security Beer-Talk: Responding to Cyber Attacks" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cULyBdtE-SM" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Compass Security Beer-Talk: Responding to Cyber Attacks"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Compass Security Beer-Talk: Responding to Cyber Attacks", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/cULyBdtE-SM\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cULyBdtE-SM", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Compass Security’s incident-response discussion</strong> complements the reporting lesson by showing why evidence, timeline, and ownership matter after an event. Use it to consider which facts a defender needs first. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Watch the discussion on YouTube"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cULyBdtE-SM"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cULyBdtE-SM" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Watch the discussion on YouTube</a> </span> .</p> <p>**The video is context, not evidence for your finding. Your report still needs its own commands, events, timestamps, and scope.</p> <h2 id="write-a-finding"> <a href="#write-a-finding" title="Write a Finding">Write a Finding</a> <a href="#write-a-finding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Write a Finding">#</a> </h2> <p>Use a <strong>finding structure</strong> which makes review quick. Put the decision first, then the evidence and limits which support it.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Title: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Objective and scope: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Observed condition: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Evidence references and timestamps: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Impact and affected owner: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Limitations and alternate explanations: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Remediation recommendation: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Remediation owner and target date: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Retest procedure and success condition: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Title</strong> should describe the condition and consequence, not a tool name. <strong>Remediation</strong> should address the weak boundary identified in the evidence. <strong>Retest</strong> should repeat the disputed operation after the fix and state what result closes the finding.</p> <h2 id="analyze-a-synthetic-finding"> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-finding" title="Analyze a Synthetic Finding">Analyze a Synthetic Finding</a> <a href="#analyze-a-synthetic-finding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Analyze a Synthetic Finding">#</a> </h2> <p>**Assume a staging Linux host uses an approved SSH certificate. The server log records a successful certificate authentication for the named assessment account. The account reads one application directory but cannot write it. No evidence shows access to production hosts or plaintext passwords.</p> <p>The <strong>supported conclusion</strong> is scoped read access to the staging directory through the configured certificate method. The report should not claim stolen passwords, production access, or domain compromise. A remediation owner narrows the account’s directory ACL or remove the certificate after the window.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence</th> <th>Supported claim</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>SSH server log</strong></td> <td>Certificate authentication occurred</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Directory read result</strong></td> <td>Named read operation succeeded</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Write denial</strong></td> <td>Named write operation was not authorized</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No production test</strong></td> <td>Production access remains untested</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No secret artifact</strong></td> <td>Plaintext collection is unsubstantiated</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="choose-remediation-and-retest"> <a href="#choose-remediation-and-retest" title="Choose Remediation and Retest">Choose Remediation and Retest</a> <a href="#choose-remediation-and-retest" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose Remediation and Retest">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>remediation</strong> should change the condition enabling the finding. Rotating an unrelated password does not repair a directory ACL. Removing a certificate without checking alternate keys or service accounts might leave the same access path open.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Finding condition</th> <th>Retest</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Unneeded certificate</strong></td> <td>Revoke it and repeat the named authentication attempt</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Excess directory read</strong></td> <td>Adjust ACL and repeat the read test</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Broad service account</strong></td> <td>Reduce scope and test each required service</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Missing logging</strong></td> <td>Enable collection and repeat the bounded action</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The retest must preserve the <strong>same objective, source, target, and operation</strong> unless the change intentionally alters one of them. Record the new result and any residual limitation.</p> <h2 id="preserve-the-timeline"> <a href="#preserve-the-timeline" title="Preserve the Timeline">Preserve the Timeline</a> <a href="#preserve-the-timeline" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Preserve the Timeline">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Timestamps</strong> connect operator actions, endpoint events, server logs, and owner decisions. Use a consistent timezone and identify clock uncertainty. An event ID without host, channel, or collection status is difficult to validate.</p> <p><strong>Evidence retention</strong> follows the engagement agreement. Keep raw records and a readable analyst extract when possible. Do not delete customer logs to make the report shorter. If data was unavailable, say which collector, host, or time range was missing.</p> <h2 id="create-the-mission-package"> <a href="#create-the-mission-package" title="Create the Mission Package">Create the Mission Package</a> <a href="#create-the-mission-package" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Mission Package">#</a> </h2> <p>Write a <strong>one-page mission finding</strong> for the synthetic SSH case. Include one alternate explanation and a retest which was able to disprove your conclusion. Identify a remediation owner and the artifact which proves closure.</p> <p><strong>Completion standard:</strong> A reviewer identifies the question, observed result, impact boundary, limitation, owner, and repeatable retest without reading the entire course.</p> <h2 id="self-check-and-answers"> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" title="Self-Check and Answers">Self-Check and Answers</a> <a href="#self-check-and-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Check and Answers">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Does SSH support prove a key is configured?</strong></td> <td>No, server configuration and logs are needed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does event 4624 prove a physical user?</strong></td> <td>No, it records a logon event with context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What belongs in limitations?</strong></td> <td>Missing collection, untested scope, and alternate explanations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What makes remediation relevant?</strong></td> <td>It changes the documented enabling condition</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What makes a retest useful?</strong></td> <td>It repeats the same disputed operation after the fix</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What closes a finding?</strong></td> <td>Owner action plus evidence meeting the success condition</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>You have completed the <strong>Red Team Course</strong> sequence. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >course hub</a> </span> to review each module, then apply the mission package format to a new approved exercise.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 3: Networking and Active Directory Foundations
item.description: The networking and Active Directory concepts every red team technique builds on: HTTP and HTTPS, TCP and UDP, the domain controller, users, groups, and group nesting.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="-return-to-the-red-team-course"> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </a> <a href="#-return-to-the-red-team-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" ← Return to the Red Team Course ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Network reachability, authentication, and authorization</strong> answer different questions. A reachable server does not prove an account is valid, and a successful login does not grant every permission. This module connects web transports, directory services, DNS, and group membership so you diagnose the right layer before choosing a tool.</p> <p><em>Allow 25 minutes for reading and 20 minutes for a small domain-lab exercise. You need basic IP addressing and access to your own Windows lab.</em></p> <h2 id="learning-outcomes"> <a href="#learning-outcomes" title="Learning Outcomes">Learning Outcomes</a> <a href="#learning-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learning Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Distinguish layers:</strong> separate an application protocol from its transport and encryption.</li> <li><strong>Explain the domain:</strong> identify the roles of DNS, a domain controller, and a resource server.</li> <li><strong>Trace permissions:</strong> follow a group-membership path to an explicit resource permission.</li> <li><strong>Interpret failure:</strong> distinguish name resolution, connection, authentication, and access denial.</li> <li><strong>Create an evidence map:</strong> connect observations without assuming a complete attack path.</li> </ul> <h2 id="protocols-have-different-jobs"> <a href="#protocols-have-different-jobs" title="Protocols Have Different Jobs">Protocols Have Different Jobs</a> <a href="#protocols-have-different-jobs" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Protocols Have Different Jobs">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>TCP</strong> provides an ordered byte stream with mechanisms for acknowledging and retransmitting data. <strong>UDP</strong> sends datagrams without TCP’s connection and delivery mechanisms. An application using UDP still implements additional reliability or security when its protocol requires it. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="TCP specification, RFC 9293"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html"> <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >TCP specification, RFC 9293</a> </span> </p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Layer</th> <th>Example</th> <th>Question it answers</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Naming</strong></td> <td>DNS</td> <td>Which address or service location corresponds to this name?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Transport</strong></td> <td>TCP or UDP</td> <td>How are bytes or datagrams carried?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Channel protection</strong></td> <td>TLS</td> <td>How is the connection authenticated and protected?</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Application</strong></td> <td>HTTP, SMB, LDAP</td> <td>What operation does the client request?</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>A port number is a clue</strong>, not proof of the application behind it. A TCP listener on port 443 still needs protocol validation. A service moved to another port keeps its application behavior, and a proxy often presents a different network endpoint from the underlying application.</p> <h2 id="http-tls-and-visibility"> <a href="#http-tls-and-visibility" title="HTTP, TLS, and Visibility">HTTP, TLS, and Visibility</a> <a href="#http-tls-and-visibility" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="HTTP, TLS, and Visibility">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>HTTPS</strong> protects HTTP traffic using a secure channel. TLS provides confidentiality and integrity for application data and supports authentication of the communicating endpoints. The protection applies between the endpoints of the TLS connection, including an inspecting proxy when one terminates the connection. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="TLS 1.3 specification, RFC 8446"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html"> <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >TLS 1.3 specification, RFC 8446</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Encryption does not establish ordinary behavior.</strong> A network observer still has connection-level information such as destination addresses, timing, and traffic volume. Endpoint tools and a configured inspection proxy have different visibility. A rarely used destination or an unusual initiating process remains relevant even when the content is encrypted.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Reasonable conclusion</th> <th>Unsupported conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>TLS negotiation succeeds</strong></td> <td>The tested TLS connection was established</td> <td>The application is trustworthy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TCP port 443 is reachable</strong></td> <td>Something accepts connections there</td> <td>All application requests will succeed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>HTTP body contains binary data</strong></td> <td>The application transfers binary content</td> <td>The transfer is malicious because it is not readable text</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No plaintext in a capture</strong></td> <td>The capture lacks clear application content</td> <td>Defenders have no other evidence</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>HTTP is not limited to text pages.</strong> Images, compressed bodies, software downloads, and application data are ordinary uses of HTTP. A claim about command-and-control traffic needs evidence from the application, endpoint, or traffic pattern, rather than a blanket assumption about binary data.</p> <p><strong>HTTP/3</strong> also corrects the shortcut “web traffic always uses TCP.” It maps HTTP semantics onto QUIC, which uses UDP. Distinguish the application protocol from its transport before interpreting a capture or proposing a firewall rule. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="HTTP/3 specification, RFC 9114"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9114.html"> <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9114.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >HTTP/3 specification, RFC 9114</a> </span> </p> <h2 id="read-a-tcp-exchange"> <a href="#read-a-tcp-exchange" title="Read a TCP Exchange">Read a TCP Exchange</a> <a href="#read-a-tcp-exchange" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Read a TCP Exchange">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Client Server </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>SYN ---------------------> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <--------------------- SYN-ACK </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ACK ---------------------> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Application data --------> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The three-way handshake</strong> establishes a TCP connection. It does not prove authentication to the application or permission to read its data. A connection failure belongs to a different diagnostic stage from a valid application response denying access.</p> <p><strong>A burst of connection attempts</strong> deserves interpretation in context. Destination count, port distribution, time interval, and the initiating application help distinguish a scan from an expected inventory job. Completing the handshake does not make scanning invisible, and a SYN scan is not inherently undetectable either.</p> <h2 id="what-active-directory-stores"> <a href="#what-active-directory-stores" title="What Active Directory Stores">What Active Directory Stores</a> <a href="#what-active-directory-stores" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What Active Directory Stores">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS)</strong> stores directory objects and supports identity, authentication, and administration for a domain environment. A <strong>domain controller (DC)</strong> runs those services and participates in directory replication. A deployment normally includes multiple domain controllers rather than a single universal database server. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft AD DS overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/get-started/virtual-dc/active-directory-domain-services-overview"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/get-started/virtual-dc/active-directory-domain-services-overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft AD DS overview</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>A domain is not a subnet.</strong> Systems in different routed networks belong to the same domain, while systems sharing a subnet belong to different domains or no domain. Separate logical identity structure from packet-routing structure in your notes.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Object or role</th> <th>Purpose</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>User account</strong></td> <td>Represents a person or application identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Computer account</strong></td> <td>Represents a domain-joined machine identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Security group</strong></td> <td>Collects principals for rights or permissions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Organizational unit</strong></td> <td>Organizes objects for delegation and policy application</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Domain controller</strong></td> <td>Provides directory and authentication services</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Resource server</strong></td> <td>Hosts the share, application, or other resource being accessed</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Domain-controller access is not every engagement’s objective.</strong> An assessment might instead test access to one application role, a file share, or an approved synthetic record. Domain controllers are sensitive dependencies, and local workstation account secrets are not simply copies of the domain account database.</p> <h2 id="dns-finds-domain-services"> <a href="#dns-finds-domain-services" title="DNS Finds Domain Services">DNS Finds Domain Services</a> <a href="#dns-finds-domain-services" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="DNS Finds Domain Services">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>DNS service records</strong> help clients locate domain controllers and domain services. A directory operation depends on more than reaching an IP address. The client also needs appropriate naming, routing, time, authentication, and permission for the requested action. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft domain-controller location process"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/dc-locator"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/dc-locator" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft domain-controller location process</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Worked failure:</strong> A workstation reaches a file server’s address but cannot resolve the domain’s service records through its configured resolver. This supports investigating DNS configuration before calling the account invalid.
